definition_en: a serious disease caused by a parasite, spread by the bites of infected mosquitoes, and marked by fever, shivering, and sweating
core_image: 沼泽上空盘旋的蚊群：一次叮咬把热病送进人的血液
scene: 古罗马人把夏日乡野的闷热、蚊虫和反复发烧看成同一件坏事，据说他们以为这种病是沼泽散出的脏气让人染上的。Doctors in the tropics test anyone with a high fever for malaria before giving treatment.
sceneCN: 这里 malaria 是「疟疾」（第 1 个义项：由疟原虫引起、经蚊虫叮咬传播的发热性疾病）；句中医生先为高烧病人做疟疾检测，再开始治疗。

derivatives.zh: 由 malaria 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「疟疾的；与疟疾有关的」
由 malaria 加表示学科的词素 -ology 构成，义为「疟疾学」
由前缀 anti-（抗、防）加 malarial 构成，义为「抗疟的；抗疟药」

senses.title: The infectious disease
senses.definition: a serious disease caused by a parasite carried by mosquitoes, marked by recurring fever, shivering, and sweating
senses.definitionCN: 由蚊子携带的疟原虫引起的严重疾病，特征是反复发作的发热、畏寒和出汗
senses.example: Millions of children still die of malaria every year.
senses.exampleCN: 每年仍有数以百万计的儿童死于疟疾。
senses.why: The word keeps only its medical sense today, but that sense still carries the root image of bad air rising from an unhealthy place.
senses.whyCN: 这个词今天只保留医学义，但这个义项仍带着「坏空气从污浊之地升起」的词根画面。

senses.title: The parasite itself
senses.definition: the microscopic parasite itself, a protozoan of the genus Plasmodium that infects red blood cells
senses.definitionCN: 指这种微小寄生物本身，即感染红细胞的疟原虫
senses.example: The microscope showed malaria parasites inside the red cells.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜显示红细胞内有疟原虫。
senses.why: Because the disease and its cause are named with the same word, scientists often use the word for the organism rather than the illness.
senses.whyCN: 因为疾病和它的病因共用一个词，科学家常直接用它指致病生物而不是病症。

senses.title: The foul air of old theory
senses.titleCN: 沼地瘴气；旧时所谓发病的空气
senses.definition: the poisoned air once thought to rise from marshes and swamps and to bring on fevers
senses.definitionCN: 旧时认为从沼泽湿地升起的、能引起发热的有毒空气
senses.example: In old medical books malaria meant the air of the marshes, not the sickness.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧医书里，malaria 指的是沼地的空气，而不是病。
senses.why: This is the literal sense the Italian phrase had, and it explains why a name made of bad air ended up attached to a mosquito born disease.
senses.whyCN: 这是意大利语短语的字面义，也解释了为什么一个由「坏空气」造出的词最终被用来指蚊媒疾病。

senses.title: The days of shivering and sweat
senses.titleCN: 寒热发作；打摆子的日子
senses.definition: the recurring attack of chills and high fever that the illness brings on in cycles
senses.definitionCN: 这种病周期性带来的寒战与高烧发作
senses.example: He could tell the fever was malaria because the shivering came every other day.
senses.exampleCN: 他凭隔天发作的寒战判断这是疟疾。
senses.why: The cycles of chills and sweats are so regular that the illness lent its name to the attacks themselves rather than staying only a label for the disease.
senses.whyCN: 寒战与出汗的周期如此规律，以至于这个词也被用来指发作本身，而不只是疾病的名称。

senses.title: A region where the disease prevails
senses.titleCN: 疟疾流行地区；疟疾之害
senses.definition: a region, climate, or condition in which the disease is widespread and harmful
senses.definitionCN: 疾病普遍流行并造成危害的地区、环境或状况
senses.example: The engineers called the flood plain a malaria zone and asked for mosquito nets.
senses.exampleCN: 工程人员把这片河漫滩称为疟疾流行区，要求配发蚊帐。
senses.why: A place name sense grew from the disease, much as conditions like damp air gave the word its origins in the first place.
senses.whyCN: 由疾病引申出对地点的指称，这与当初湿气一类环境催生这个词的情形正好相映。

intro.en: Malaria comes from Italian mala aria, meaning bad air, because people once believed the illness was carried by the foul air of marshes; the modern cause was found much later.
intro.cn: malaria 来自意大利语 mala aria，意思是「坏空气」，因为人们曾以为这种病由沼泽的污浊空气带来；真正病因要到很久以后才被发现。

items.en: Malus means bad, and aer or air is the Latin word for air.
items.cn: malus 意为坏的，aer（或写作 air）是拉丁语中表示空气的词。

items.en: The phrase mala aria, literally bad air, is used for the unhealthy air of the Roman Campagna.
items.cn: mala aria 字面即「坏空气」，十八世纪时用来指罗马乡野那种不健康的空气。

items.en: The English word malaria first appears as a name for the feverish illness linked to those southern districts.
items.cn: 英语 malaria 最初指与意大利南部地区有关的发热病。

items.en: As the miasma theory faded, the word settled on the disease itself rather than the air.
items.cn: 随着瘴气说衰落，这个词从空气转向疾病本身。

items.en: The parasite now called Plasmodium was seen by Laveran in 1880, and only then was the real cause named.
items.cn: 一八八〇年拉韦朗看到后来称为疟原虫的寄生物，真正病因才被命名。

items.en: Malaria now names both the disease and its parasite, and the old air theory survives only in the etymology.
items.cn: 现代英语中 malaria 既指疾病也指病原，旧的空气说只留在词源里。

note.en: Malaria is a medical word built on the Latin root mal- for bad, close to other mal- words and to the fever conditions once blamed on bad air.
note.cn: malaria 是建立在拉丁词根 mal-（坏）之上的医学术语，与其它 mal- 词以及旧时归咎于坏空气的热病名称相邻。

entries.definition: a general feeling of being unwell
entries.definitionCN: 不适；浑身不舒服（与 malaria 同用 mal-，但来自法语，义为身体不适）

entries.definition: a disease or illness
entries.definitionCN: 疾病；病痛（与 malaria 同用拉丁坏 root，这里指较正式的疾病）

entries.definition: of or caused by malaria
an old word for a fever with regular shivering fits
entries.definitionCN: 寒热病；旧时指有规律寒战的发烧（旧称，常用于历史上的疟疾记载）

entries.definition: a mosquito borne viral fever with severe pain
entries.definitionCN: 登革热（同为蚊媒热病，由病毒而非疟原虫引起）

entries.definition: a viral fever spread by mosquitoes in the tropics
entries.definitionCN: 黄热病（同为热带蚊媒热病，可预防）

normalIntro.en: Split malaria into mal-, bad, and aria, air, and remember that a bad air word became a mosquito disease.
normalIntro.cn: 把 malaria 拆成 mal-（坏）和 aria（空气），记住这个「坏空气」词后来变成了蚊媒疾病。

normal.en: Mal- means bad in Latin, so malaria once meant bad air.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mal- 意为坏的，所以 malaria 曾指坏空气。

normal.en: The second part echoes the Latin word for air, aria.
normal.cn: 后半部分让人想起拉丁语中表示空气的 aria。

normal.en: Malaria is spread by mosquitoes, not by foul air.
normal.cn: 疟疾由蚊子传播，不是由污浊空气传播。

normal.en: Contract malaria means to catch the disease.
normal.cn: contract malaria 表示染上疟疾。

normal.en: Malarial is the adjective, as in malarial fever.
normal.cn: malarial 是形容词，如 malarial fever。

abstract.en: See a sheet of mist rising off a swamp at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时沼泽上升起一片雾气。

abstract.en: Hear a mosquito whine close to an ear, then fever and shivering.
abstract.cn: 想象蚊子贴着耳边嗡嗡作响，接着高烧与寒战来袭。

abstract.en: Feel the chill and sweat coming back every other day.
abstract.cn: 感受隔天就轮回一次的寒战与大汗。

examples.en: Malaria is still one of the leading causes of death in tropical regions.
examples.cn: 疟疾至今仍是热带地区的主要死因之一。

examples.en: She took pills every day to protect herself from malaria.
examples.cn: 她每天服药以防疟疾。

examples.en: Scientists hope a new vaccine will reduce malarial infections in children.
examples.cn: 科学界希望一种新疫苗能减少儿童疟疾感染。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马来热」——去马来一带旅行要防的「热病」，就是疟疾；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 意大利语 mala（坏的）+ aria（空气）→ malaria，本义「坏空气」，指罗马沼泽地带可致发热的空气；1880 年发现病原后，词义转为「疟疾」。

sensesIntro.en: Malaria grew from a phrase for bad air into a name for the disease, and then spread to the parasite, the old air theory, the bouts of fever, and the regions where it endures.
sensesIntro.cn: malaria 从「坏空气」的短语演变为疾病名称，再扩展到病原、旧时空气说、发热发作以及病魔肆虐的地区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: mist rising from a marsh, said to carry fever.
core.cn: 核心意象：沼泽升起雾气，据说带着热病。

branches.en: The infectious disease is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 这种传染病是现代核心义项。

branches.en: The parasite sense names the organism behind the disease.
branches.cn: 疟原虫义项指疾病背后的生物。

branches.en: The bad air sense preserves the literal Italian phrase.
branches.cn: 瘴气义项保留意大利语短语的字面意思。

branches.en: The chills and fever sense points to the attacks of the illness.
branches.cn: 寒热发作义项指疾病一轮轮的发作。

branches.en: The regional sense extends the disease to places and conditions where it lasts.
branches.cn: 地区义项把疾病延伸到长期流行的地点与状况。

intro.en: Malaria is a compound of Latin malus, bad, and aer, air, with English relatives built on the same bad root.
intro.cn: malaria 由拉丁语 malus（坏的）与 aer（空气）组合而成，英语中围绕同一个「坏」词根还衍生出若干相关词。

latinIntro.en: Latin malus means bad and aer means air; the Italian phrase mala aria joins them literally.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 malus 意为坏的，aer 意为空气；意大利语短语 mala aria 就是把二者直接拼合。

items.example: Mal- is the bad element in malaria.
items.exampleCN: mal- 是 malaria 中表示「坏」的成分。

items.example: Aria is the air part of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: aria 是短语中表示「空气」的部分。

items.example: Mala aria was blamed for fevers.
items.exampleCN: mala aria 曾被归咎为热病的成因。

items.example: Malaria is the direct borrowing.
items.exampleCN: malaria 是直接借来的词形。

items.example: The suffix -al forms malarial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 malarial。

items.example: Malaise shares the same bad root.
items.exampleCN: malaise 共享同一个「坏」词根。

items.example: Malady shares the same bad root.
items.exampleCN: malady 共享同一个「坏」词根。

items.example: The prefix anti- forms antimalarial.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 anti- 构成 antimalarial。

items.example: Antimalarial drugs save lives.
items.exampleCN: 抗疟药能救命。

definition_zh: 不满的；不满者；不满分子
definition_en: discontented with the way things are, especially with authority, and often a person who complains or rebels
core_image: 紧皱眉头、抱着双臂站在人群外围的一个人，什么都没让他满意
scene: 镇上的粮食价格连连上涨，一部分居民开始私下聚会，对镇长和外来的征税官冷言冷语。The malcontent farmers demanded lower taxes and a fairer share of the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 malcontent 是「不满的」（第 1 个义项：对现状、尤其对当权者心怀不满），句中也指这样一群不满的人；句中不满的农民要求减税，并要求更公平的收成分配。

pos.zh: 不满者；不满分子；对现状心怀不满的人

derivatives.zh: 由 malcontent 加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「不满的；爱抱怨的」
由 malcontent 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「不满情绪」
由 malcontented 加 -ly 构成，义为「不满地；悻悻地」

senses.title: Dissatisfied with things as they are
senses.definition: feeling unhappy and dissatisfied, usually because one thinks things are unfair or badly run
senses.definitionCN: 感到不开心、不满意，通常认为事情不公或管理糟糕
senses.example: Malcontent villagers gathered outside the council office.
senses.exampleCN: 心怀不满的村民聚集在议事厅外。
senses.why: The Latin prefix mal-, bad, joins content, satisfied, so the word pictures a person for whom the good has gone bad.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 mal-（坏）与 content（满足）结合，画面是一个原本满意的人被「坏」掉了。

senses.title: The chronically complaining person
senses.titleCN: 不满者；尤指爱抱怨的人
senses.definition: a person who is habitually dissatisfied and keeps complaining about the way things are
senses.definitionCN: 长期不满、对现状不断抱怨的人
senses.example: He is a malcontent who finds fault with every new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 他总是不满，对每项新规定都要挑刺。
senses.why: Used of a person, the adjective became a noun and named the kind of person who carries that mood about.
senses.whyCN: 用于指人时，形容词转化为名词，也命中了那种把不满挂在身上的人。

senses.title: One who opposes the ruling power
senses.definition: a person who is dissatisfied with, and openly critical of, a government or ruler
senses.definitionCN: 对政府或统治者不满并公开批评的人
senses.example: The king ordered his guards to watch the known malcontents.
senses.exampleCN: 国王命令卫兵监视那些已知的不满分子。
senses.why: In political history the word took on a sharper edge and labelled critics of rulers as a suspicious crowd.
senses.whyCN: 在政治史中这个词带上更锐利的色彩，把批评统治者的人标成可疑的一群。

senses.title: The restless, uneasy mood
senses.titleCN: 不满的情绪；闹别扭的状态
senses.definition: a mood of dull dissatisfaction that lingers without a clear cause
senses.definitionCN: 一种持续存在、没有明确缘由的闷闷不满情绪
senses.example: A wave of malcontent spread through the factory after the pay cut.
senses.exampleCN: 减薪以后，一阵不满情绪在工厂里蔓延开来。
senses.why: The abstract sense extends the feeling from persons to a whole group or place, where dissatisfaction hangs like weather.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把这种情绪从个人扩展到群体或场所，不满就像天气一样笼罩在那里。

senses.title: A long standing grievance against a state
senses.definition: a settled, long held complaint against a country or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 对国家或组织长期积压的怨气
senses.example: Every century has had its malcontent against the crown.
senses.exampleCN: 每个世纪都有人对王权怀着长期的怨怼。
senses.why: Politically, the word can name an ongoing stance toward power rather than a passing mood.
senses.whyCN: 在政治上，这个词也可以指对权力的一种长期立场，而不只是短时的心情。

intro.en: Malcontent joins Latin malus, bad, and content, satisfied, in the sixteenth century, when the English word named those discontented with the state.
intro.cn: malcontent 由拉丁语 malus（坏的）与 content（满足）在十六世纪合成，当时指对国家与政府不满的人。

items.en: Malus means bad and contentus means satisfied.
items.cn: malus 意为坏的，contentus 意为满足的。

items.en: Content enters English from French with the sense of satisfied.
items.cn: content 经由法语进入英语，意为满足的。

items.en: Malcontent is first recorded in the sixteenth century as a name for the dissatisfied.
items.cn: 十六世纪最早记载 malcontent，用来称呼不满的人。

items.en: The word is widely used of those who resent a king or a government.
items.cn: 十七世纪时广泛用于指怨恨国王或政府的人。

items.en: Today it can still be an adjective, though the noun form is the more common one.
items.cn: 今天它仍可作形容词，但名词形式更常用。

note.en: Malcontent is a mal- compound sharing its root with malaise and malady, and it stands close to the ordinary words for dissatisfaction and rebellion.
note.cn: malcontent 是 mal- 复合词，与 malaise、malady 同根，并与表示不满与反抗的普通词语义相邻。

entries.definition: a vague feeling of unease
entries.definitionCN: 不适；莫名的不安（只是与 malcontent 共享 mal- 词头，词源不同）

entries.definition: an illness
entries.definitionCN: 疾病（与 malcontent 共享 mal-，此处指病痛）

entries.definition: harmful, evil
entries.definitionCN: 恶性的；恶意的（与 malcontent 共享 mal-，此处指有害）

entries.definition: unhappy with the state of things
not pleased with something
no longer loyal to an authority
entries.definitionCN: 对当局不再忠心的；心怀不满的

normalIntro.en: Malcontent is mal-, bad, plus content, satisfied, so it reads as badly satisfied.
normalIntro.cn: malcontent 是 mal-（坏）加 content（满足），读起来就是「被弄得不满足了」。

normal.en: Content means satisfied, so malcontent means satisfied no longer.
normal.cn: content 意为满足，所以 malcontent 就是不再满足。

normal.en: Mal- for bad appears in malaise, malady, and malpractice.
normal.cn: 表示「坏」的 mal- 也出现在 malaise、malady 与 malpractice 里。

normal.en: As a noun, malcontent means a dissatisfied person.
normal.cn: 作名词时，malcontent 指不满的人。

normal.en: A malcontent often complains about the government.
normal.cn: 不满者常常抱怨政府。

normal.en: Compare contented, the satisfied opposite.
normal.cn: 对比 contented，那是表示满足的反义说法。

abstract.en: Squeeze a smiling face into a sour frown.
abstract.cn: 想象一张笑脸被挤成一张苦脸。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing apart, arms folded, saying nothing pleases them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人叉着手站在一旁，说没什么能让他满意。

abstract.en: Hear a low grumble that never quite stops.
abstract.cn: 想象一声始终停不下来的低声咕哝。

examples.en: The malcontent crowd refused to leave the square.
examples.cn: 不满的人群拒绝离开广场。

examples.en: She was a malcontent who never trusted any minister.
examples.cn: 她是一个不满者，从不信任任何部长。

examples.en: Officials blamed a few malcontents for stirring up trouble.
examples.cn: 官员们把挑事的责任归到少数不满分子身上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖了坑人」——被人「卖」在「坑」里，心里当然不满足，于是成了不满者；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 malus（坏的）+ contentus（满足的）→ 英语 content（满足）+ mal-（坏）→ malcontent，核心义「把满足弄坏了的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Malcontent starts as the adjective for being dissatisfied, turns into the name for a dissatisfied person, hardens into the political critic, then loosens into a lasting mood and long held grievance.
sensesIntro.cn: malcontent 先是表示「不满的」形容词，再转为不满者，政治色彩加重后成为批评当权者的人，最后又泛化为持续的情绪与长期的怨怼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sour face at the edge of a crowd, satisfied with nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群边上那张苦脸，对什么都不满意。

branches.en: The adjective states the feeling of dissatisfaction.
branches.cn: 形容词义项表明不满的感受。

branches.en: The noun names the person who keeps complaining.
branches.cn: 名词义项指不断抱怨的人。

branches.en: The political sense names a critic of the ruling power.
branches.cn: 政治义项指批评当权者的人。

branches.en: A personal feeling can spread into the mood of a whole group.
branches.cn: 个人的感受可以蔓延成整个群体的情绪。

branches.en: Political criticism can settle into a long held grievance.
branches.cn: 政治批评可以沉淀为长期的怨怼。

intro.en: Malcontent is built from the Latin bad root mal- and the English word content, and it has English relatives in the same family.
intro.cn: malcontent 由拉丁「坏」词根 mal- 与英语词 content 构成，同一词族中还有其它英语亲属词。

latinIntro.en: Latin malus gives the bad element and contentus, satisfied, gives the rest of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 malus 提供「坏」的成分，contentus（满足的）提供其余部分。

items.example: Mal- shows the bad turn taken.
items.exampleCN: mal- 表示「坏」的转向。

items.example: Content is the satisfied half.
items.exampleCN: content 是表示「满足」的那一半。

items.example: Malcontent names the sour mood.
items.exampleCN: malcontent 描摹这股酸涩情绪。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms malcontented.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 malcontented。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ment forms malcontentment.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 malcontentment。

items.example: The prefix dis- negates content.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 dis- 否定 content。

items.example: Dissatisfied is the plainer synonym.
items.exampleCN: dissatisfied 是更朴素的近义词。

items.example: Malaise shares the bad root.

definition_zh: 恶意的；狠毒的；幸灾乐祸的
definition_en: wishing or showing harm to others, with a cold desire to see them suffer
core_image: 阴影里一个人冷冷地注视着别人跌倒，嘴角浮起一丝满意的笑
scene: 走廊尽头，那个同事看到有人被解雇的消息，不但没有同情，反而泛起了快意的笑容。The old man gave a malevolent look as the children ran past his gate.
sceneCN: 这里 malevolent 是「恶意的」（第 1 个义项：希望他人受苦并为此感到快意）；句中老人看孩子们跑过门口时投去恶意的目光。

pos.zh: 恶意的；狠毒的；希望他人受害的

derivatives.zh: 由 malevolent 变 -ent 为 -ence 构成，义为「恶意；狠毒」
由 malevolent 加词尾 -ly 构成，义为「恶意地」
由拉丁词根 bene-（好）替换 mal- 构成，义为「仁慈的；乐善好施的」

senses.title: Wishing harm on others
senses.titleCN: 恶意的；希望他人受害的
senses.definition: having a wish or a wishful attitude that others should suffer
senses.definitionCN: 怀着希望别人受苦的心意或态度
senses.example: He gave her a malevolent glance as she left.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开时，他投来恶意的目光。
senses.why: Latin male, badly, joins velle, to wish, so the adjective literally means wishing badly for others.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 male（坏地）与 velle（愿望）结合，字面就是「愿望朝坏处走」，即对他人怀有恶愿。

senses.title: Intending to do harm
senses.definition: planning or acting with the clear aim of causing harm
senses.definitionCN: 有明确害人目的的计划或行动
senses.example: The malevolent plan aimed to ruin the charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这个狠毒的计划意图毁掉那家慈善机构。
senses.why: The same wishing root extends from the inner wish to the outward plan, so the harm is done by design rather than by accident.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「意愿」的词根，从内心之愿延伸到外在的谋划，所以这种伤害是有意而非偶然造成的。

senses.title: The look that gloats at trouble
senses.titleCN: 幸灾乐祸的；透着快意的冷眼
senses.definition: showing a cold, satisfied pleasure at the trouble of another
senses.definitionCN: 他人遭难时露出冷淡而满足的快意
senses.example: There was a malevolent smile on his face when the rival failed.
senses.exampleCN: 对手失败时，他脸上挂着幸灾乐祸的笑。
senses.why: A face can carry the wish without doing anything, so the word also describes looks and smiles that enjoy the fall of another.
senses.whyCN: 一张脸即使什么都不做也能显出这种心愿，所以这个词也形容享受他人跌落的眼光与笑容。

senses.title: Said of curses, powers, or spirits
senses.definition: describing a curse, power, or spirit thought to bring evil on people
senses.definitionCN: 形容被认为会给人们带来灾祸的诅咒、力量或神灵
senses.example: The plot blames a malevolent ghost for the strange deaths.
senses.exampleCN: 小说把那些离奇死亡归咎于一个恶灵。
senses.why: Old story and belief carry the wish for harm onto invisible beings, so the word came to colour curses and spirits too.
senses.whyCN: 古老的传说把一个「害人之愿」寄托在无形的存在上，于是这个词也带上了诅咒与神灵的色彩。

senses.title: Said of hostile power or writing
senses.definition: describing a speech, review, or force that is full of hostility
senses.definitionCN: 形容充满敌意的言辞、评论或势力
senses.example: The paper published a malevolent attack on the new law.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸发表了一篇恶意攻击新法律的评论。
senses.why: When people pour hostility into words or institutions, the same root word describes the work rather than a face.
senses.whyCN: 当人们把敌意倾注到文字或体制中时，同一个词根词就用来形容这些作品，而不是一张脸。

intro.en: Malevolent comes from Latin male, badly, and velle, to wish, literally wishing badly for someone.
intro.cn: malevolent 来自拉丁语 male（坏地）与 velle（愿望），字面意思是「为别人许下坏愿」。

items.en: Male means badly and velle means to wish.
items.cn: male 意为坏地，velle 意为愿望。

items.en: The adjective malevolens describes a person who is ill disposed toward others.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 malevolens 指对他人心怀恶意的人。

items.en: Malevolent is borrowed into English as the opposite of benevolent.
items.cn: malevolent 作为 benevolent 的反义被借入英语。

items.en: The word widens to describe curses, spirits, and hostile writing.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词的用法扩展到诅咒、神灵与敌意文字。

items.en: Today it most often describes a look, a smile, or a force that plans or enjoys harm.
items.cn: 今天它最常形容谋划或享受他人受害的目光、笑容或力量。

note.en: Malevolent is a mal- word sharing its root with malaise and malignant, and it stands opposite benevolent, the same Latin pattern with the good prefix.
note.cn: malevolent 是 mal- 词，与 malaise、malignant 同根，并与 benevolent 相对；后者用同样句式，只是把前缀换成了表示好的 bene-。

kind and wishing good to others

entries.definition: harmful and evil

showing bitter desire to hurt
cruel and violent

normalIntro.en: Malevolent is male, badly, and volent, wishing, the exact mirror of benevolent, wishing well.
normalIntro.cn: malevolent 由 male（坏地）与 volent（愿望）组成，正是 benevolent（许好愿）的镜像。

normal.en: Latin male means badly and velle means to wish.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 male 意为坏地，velle 意为愿望。

normal.en: Benevolent wishes well and malevolent wishes harm.
normal.cn: benevolent 许好愿，malevolent 许恶愿。

normal.en: The noun is malevolence, the quality of such a wish.
normal.cn: 名词是 malevolence，指这种恶愿的性质。

normal.en: A malevolent look gives no help and no sympathy.
normal.cn: 恶意的目光既不给帮助也不给同情。

normal.en: Malevolent is stronger and more literary than bad.
normal.cn: malevolent 比 bad 更重，也更书面。

abstract.en: Picture a face in the shadow smiling when someone falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一张藏在阴影里的脸，在别人跌倒时微笑。

abstract.en: Imagine a letter of good wishes with every word crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一封祝福信被逐字划掉。

abstract.en: Think of a cold draft that follows you down a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵冷风跟在你身后穿过幽暗走廊。

examples.en: The film gives the villain a malevolent smile.
examples.cn: 电影给了反派一个恶毒的笑。

examples.en: Her malevolent remarks upset the whole team.
examples.cn: 她那些带着恶意的评论让整个团队很不快。

examples.en: Some legends describe a malevolent spirit that steals children.
examples.cn: 有些传说描写一个偷走孩子的恶灵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「魔鬼了」——心里住进了「魔鬼」，于是生出恶意；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 male（坏地）+ velle（愿望）→ malevolens（心怀恶意的）→ 英语 malevolent，与 benevolent（许好愿）相对，核心义「愿望朝坏处走」。

sensesIntro.en: Malevolent spreads from the inner wish for harm to the plan that carries it out, then to gloating looks, evil spirits, and hostile words or forces.
sensesIntro.cn: malevolent 从内心害人的愿望，扩展到实施它的谋划，再到幸灾乐祸的眼神、恶灵，以及敌意的言辞或势力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cold smile in shadow watching another person fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：阴影里那抹冷笑，看着别人跌倒。

branches.en: The inner wish for harm is the root sense.
branches.cn: 内心害人的愿望是根本义项。

branches.en: A planned harm turns the wish into action.
branches.cn: 蓄意加害把愿望变成行动。

branches.en: A gloating face shows the wish without acting.
branches.cn: 幸灾乐祸的脸不动手也显出这种愿望。

branches.en: Curses and spirits carry the harm wish into the unseen world.
branches.cn: 诅咒与神灵把害人的愿望带进看不见的世界。

branches.en: Hostile writing and malevolent plans both attack by design.
branches.cn: 充满敌意的文字与恶毒的计划都是蓄意进攻。

intro.en: Malevolent is built from Latin elements for badly and wishing, and its English relatives form a small family around the mal- root.
intro.cn: malevolent 由拉丁语中表示「坏地」与「愿望」的成分构成，英语中围绕 mal- 词根还有一小群亲属词。

latinIntro.en: Latin male means badly and velle means to wish, exactly as bene and velle give benevolent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 male 意为坏地，velle 意为愿望，正如 bene 与 velle 组成 benevolent。
