items.exampleCN: male- 提供「坏」的方向。

items.example: The element -volent comes from velle.
items.exampleCN: -volent 这一成分来自 velle。

items.example: Malevolent mirrors benevolent.
items.exampleCN: malevolent 与 benevolent 成镜像。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ence forms malevolence.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ence 构成 malevolence。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms malevolently.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 malevolently。

items.example: Bene- is the good opposite of male-.
items.exampleCN: bene- 是 male- 的反义「好」。

items.example: Benevolent is the good twin.
items.exampleCN: benevolent 是善良的双胞胎。

items.example: Malign shares the bad root.
items.exampleCN: malign 共享「坏」这个词根。

definition_zh: 畸形；发育缺陷；结构缺陷；变形；构造缺陷
definition_en: a fault in the way something is formed, especially a body part or organ that develops wrongly
core_image: 原本应当匀称成形的器官或机件，在成型那一刻长成了歪斜的形状
scene: 产科超声检查的画面里，医生指着屏幕上的一处凹陷，向紧张的父母解释这属于先天性结构缺陷。On the ultrasound monitor the doctor pointed to a small indentation in the babys spine and described it as a malformation that would need surgery.
sceneCN: 这里 malformation 是「先天性畸形」（第 1 个义项：身体部位在胚胎发育中形成的结构缺陷）；句意为医生在超声屏幕上指出婴儿脊柱的一处小凹陷，称之为需要手术矫正的畸形。

pos.zh: 畸形；发育缺陷；结构缺陷；变形

derivatives.zh: 畸形的基础词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「畸形的；形状有缺陷的」
去掉否定前缀 mal- 后的基础名词，义为「形成；构成；形成物」
不同词根的同义名词，义为「畸形；缺陷」，侧重外观异常

senses.title: A birth defect in a body part
senses.titleCN: 先天性畸形：身体部位发育异常
senses.definition: a condition in which a body part or organ develops in the wrong shape, often present from birth
senses.definitionCN: 身体部位或器官发育成错误形状的情况，通常在出生时即已存在
senses.example: The scan revealed a malformation in the babys heart.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描发现婴儿心脏有畸形。
senses.why: The Latin prefix mal- adds the idea of wrongness to formation, so a malformation is a body built along the wrong line during development.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 mal- 给 formation 加上了「错误」的意思，所以畸形就是在发育过程中沿错误路线长成的身体部位。

senses.title: A faulty structure in an object
senses.titleCN: 结构缺陷：物体的构造错误
senses.definition: an irregular or faulty shape or structure in an object or a machine part
senses.definitionCN: 物体或机件上不规则、有缺陷的形状或结构
senses.example: Engineers traced the crack to a malformation in the wing frame.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把裂纹追溯到机翼框架的一处结构缺陷。
senses.why: The same wrong formation can apply to anything made, so the word extends from bodies to parts and structures.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「错误成型」也能用在任何被制造的东西上，于是这个词从身体扩展到零件与建筑结构。

senses.title: The process of forming wrongly
senses.definition: the act or process of shaping something into a wrong form
senses.definitionCN: 把某物塑造成错误形状的行为或过程
senses.example: Heat during the casting stage causes malformation of the alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 铸造阶段的高温会导致合金变形。
senses.why: The suffix -ation names an action or process, so the word can describe the very act of forming wrongly, not only its result.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ation 表示动作或过程，因此这个词也能描述「错误成型」这一动作本身，而不只是其结果。

senses.title: A description judged abnormal
senses.definition: a feature that people judge to be abnormal, ugly or badly shaped
senses.definitionCN: 被人们判为异常、难看或形状糟糕的特征
senses.example: Critics called the new building a malformation.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这座新建筑称作畸形之物。
senses.why: Because mal- also carries the sense of bad, the word can be a judgement rather than a medical fact.
senses.whyCN: 因为 mal- 也带有「坏」的意思，这个词可以是一种评判，而不只是医学事实。

senses.title: A faulty plan or arrangement
senses.definition: a badly arranged plan, system or set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 安排糟糕的计划、制度或规则
senses.example: Histories often blame the malformation of the new tax rules.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家常责怪新税则的制定存在缺陷。
senses.why: Once formation is read abstractly as arrangement, a malformation becomes a faulty design of rules or plans.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把 formation 抽象理解为「安排」，畸形就变成了规则或计划设计上的缺陷。

senses.title: A malformed word or phrase
senses.titleCN: 语言学中的不规范构词
senses.definition: in linguistics, a word or phrase that has not been formed according to the rules of the language
senses.definitionCN: 语言学术语，指未按语言规则构造的词语或短语
senses.example: The linguist listed the malformation as an illegal compound.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家把这个不规范构词列为不合法的复合词。
senses.why: Linguistics borrows formation for how words are built, so a malformation is a word built against the rules.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用 formation 表示「词的构造」，所以畸形构词就是违反规则造出来的词。

intro.en: Malformation joins the Latin prefix malus, bad, to formare, to shape, and reaches English through the French form- family in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: malformation 把拉丁语表「坏」的 malus 与表「塑形」的 formare 结合起来，经十八世纪法语中 form- 词族进入英语。

items.en: Malus means bad, and the same stem supplies the negative prefix mal-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 malus 意为「坏的」，也为否定前缀 mal- 提供来源。

items.en: Formare means to shape or mould, and forma means a shape.
items.cn: formare 意为塑形、塑造，forma 意为形状。

items.en: The French form- family supplies the building blocks for the noun.
items.cn: 法语中 form- 词族为这个名词提供构词材料。

items.en: The word is recorded from the eighteenth century, first in scientific and medical writing.
items.cn: 这个词自十八世纪起有文献记录，最初见于科学与医学写作。

items.en: Medicine made it a standard term for a defect that appears at birth, while engineering and linguistics added their own uses.
items.cn: 医学把它变成表示出生缺陷的标准术语，工程与语言学又各自增加了用法。

note.en: Malformation shares the form- family with formation, malformed and reform, and sits beside medical defect words such as deformity and abnormality.
note.cn: malformation 与 formation、malformed、reform 同属 form- 词族，又与 deformity、abnormality 等医学缺陷词相邻。

entries.definition: the process of forming or a thing formed
entries.definitionCN: 形成；构成；形成物，是去掉否定前缀后的基础名词

entries.definition: badly or wrongly shaped
a failure to work properly
entries.definitionCN: 故障；失灵，与目标词共享表示坏的前缀

entries.definition: a malformed body part or its shape
entries.definitionCN: 畸形；缺陷，侧重外观异常，词根不同

entries.definition: something that is not normal in a body or system
entries.definitionCN: 异常；异常情况，是医学上更宽的术语

entries.definition: a fault or lack in something produced or made
entries.definitionCN: 缺陷；瑕疵，泛指任何不足或毛病

normalIntro.en: Malformation is built from the Latin word for bad and the Latin word for shaping, plus the noun ending that names the result.
normalIntro.cn: malformation 由拉丁语表「坏」的词与表「塑形」的词构成，再加上表示结果的名词词尾。

normal.en: The prefix mal- means bad: compare malice, malfunction and malnutrition.
normal.cn: 前缀 mal- 表示「坏」：对比 malice、malfunction 与 malnutrition。

normal.en: The root form- means shape: compare formation, form and reform.
normal.cn: 词根 form- 表示「形状」：对比 formation、form 与 reform。

normal.en: The suffix -ation turns the act of forming into a concrete result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ation 把「成型」这一动作变成具体结果。

normal.en: The adjective malformed drops the noun ending and adds -ed.
normal.cn: 形容词 malformed 去掉名词词尾，加上 -ed。

normal.en: Compare congenital malformation, a set phrase in medical writing about defects present at birth.
normal.cn: 对比 congenital malformation，这是医学写作中关于先天缺陷的固定搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a potter pressing clay into shape, but the thumbs pinch one side too thin.
abstract.cn: 想象陶匠把黏土压成形，可是一根拇指把一侧捏得太薄。

abstract.en: Imagine a gear cut with one tooth off centre, so the whole machine hums and shakes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个齿轮被切偏了一个齿，整台机器因此嗡嗡作响、不停抖动。

abstract.en: See a word squeezed out of two odd parts that do not fit, and grammar marks it red.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词由两个凑不到一起的部分硬挤而成，语法检查把它标成红色。

examples.en: Doctors detected a congenital malformation during the first scan.
examples.cn: 医生在第一次扫描时发现了先天性畸形。

examples.en: A malformation in the gearbox forced the firm to recall the cars.
examples.cn: 变速箱的一处结构缺陷迫使公司召回汽车。

examples.en: The journal reports that pollution may be linked to malformations in fish.
examples.cn: 该期刊报告称污染可能与鱼类畸形有关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「毛福美神」——好端端的形状被弄坏了，歪在那里：畸形；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mal-（坏，源自 malus）+ formare（塑形，源自 forma 形状）+ -ation（名词词尾），经法语 form- 词族进入十八世纪英语，核心义「成型时搞歪了」。

sensesIntro.en: Malformation starts as a body built in the wrong shape, then spreads to faulty objects, the act of forming wrongly, judgements of ugliness, badly arranged systems and illegal words.
sensesIntro.cn: malformation 最初指长歪了的身体部位，随后扩展到有缺陷的物件、错误成型的过程、对难看的评判、安排糟糕的制度以及不规范的构词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body part that should be even is moulded along the wrong line and comes out crooked.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该匀称的身体部位沿着错误的线被塑造成型，结果长歪了。

branches.en: The body line: a defect present from birth is the central medical sense.
branches.cn: 身体线：出生即存在的缺陷是最核心的医学义项。

branches.en: The machine line: the same wrong shape appears in parts and structures.
branches.cn: 机械线：同样的错误形状出现在零件与建筑结构中。

branches.en: The process line: the noun ending lets the word name the act of forming wrongly.
branches.cn: 过程线：名词词尾让这个词可以指「错误成型」的动作本身。

branches.en: The judgement line: ugly shape becomes a matter of taste rather than medicine.
branches.cn: 评判线：难看的形状从医学问题变成审美判断。

branches.en: The design and language lines: systems and words can also be built against the rules.
branches.cn: 设计与语言线：制度与词语也可能违反规则地被构造出来。

intro.en: Malformation is the negative prefix mal- plus the Latin shaping root, with English endings that build formation, malformed and the related term malfunction.
intro.cn: malformation 是表否定的前缀 mal- 加上拉丁语「塑形」词根，再配英语词尾，扩展出 formation、malformed 以及相关的 malfunction。

latinIntro.en: Latin malus means bad, and formare means to shape, so the compound names a bad shaping.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 malus 意为「坏」，formare 意为「塑形」，所以这个复合词表达的是「糟糕的塑形」。

items.example: The prefix mal- marks something as bad.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mal- 把某物标为「坏」。

items.example: Formare gives the shaping idea.
items.exampleCN: formare 提供「塑形」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms formation and malformation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 formation 与 malformation。

items.meaning: the process of forming or a thing formed
items.example: Formation is the neutral noun of shaping.
items.exampleCN: formation 是表示「塑形」的中性名词。

items.example: Malformed describes the result of the bad shaping.
items.exampleCN: malformed 描述错误塑形的结果。

items.example: Malformation keeps both the medical and the general sense.
items.exampleCN: malformation 同时保留医学与一般含义。

items.example: Reform shows the same root with the prefix re-.
items.exampleCN: reform 显示同一词根配前缀 re-。

items.example: Malfunction shares mal- but not the root.
items.exampleCN: malfunction 共享 mal-，但词根不同。

items.meaning: to spoil the shape of something
items.example: Deform is the near synonym built with de-.
items.exampleCN: deform 是用前缀 de- 构成的近义词。

definition_zh: 恶意；怨恨；蓄意伤害（法律）；恶意的意图
definition_en: the desire to harm someone or to make them suffer, especially in a deliberate and unprovoked way
core_image: 抿起的嘴角背后藏着一把看不见的刀，表面客气，心里却定好了要伤人
scene: 法庭上，辩护律师坚称被告只是失手，控方却拿出短信记录，证明他事先就存有伤害对方的恶意，属于蓄意行为。The prosecutor argued that the messages proved malice, because the defendant had planned the attack for weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 malice 是「蓄意伤害的恶意」（第 1 个义项：想让他人受害或痛苦的意图）；句意为控方主张这些短信证明被告怀有蓄意伤人的恶意，因为他已筹划了数周。

pos.zh: 恶意；怨恨；蓄意伤害的意图

derivatives.zh: 基础词加形容词后缀 -ious 构成，义为「恶意的；蓄意伤人的」
malicious 再加副词后缀 -ly，义为「恶意地；蓄意地」
同一拉丁词源分支，义为「恶毒的；诽谤」，与 malice 词源相邻
同源形容词，本义「怀有恶意的」，医学中义为「恶性的」

senses.title: A desire to harm others
senses.titleCN: 恶意：想伤害他人的念头
senses.definition: the wish to hurt another person or to see them suffer
senses.definitionCN: 想伤害他人或看他受苦的心愿
senses.example: She spoke without malice, though her words stung.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话并无恶意，尽管那些话很扎人。
senses.why: Latin mal- means bad, and malice is the bad thing living in the mind before any hand moves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mal- 表示「坏」，malice 就是动手之前先住在心里的那点「坏」。

senses.title: The intention to do harm
senses.definition: in law, the deliberate intention to commit a wrongful act that harms someone
senses.definitionCN: 法律上所指故意实施伤害他人之行为的意图
senses.example: The charge requires proof of malice on the part of the accused.
senses.exampleCN: 这项指控需要证明被告一方具有蓄意伤害的意图。
senses.why: Law turns the inner wish into a fact it must prove, so malice becomes the deliberate part of an act.
senses.whyCN: 法律把内心的念头变成必须证明的事实，于是恶意成了行为中「故意」的那一部分。

senses.title: Spite or bitter resentment
senses.definition: a lasting feeling of resentment that makes someone want to get even
senses.definitionCN: 持久的怨恨，使某人想要报复
senses.example: He bore malice against his old rival for years.
senses.exampleCN: 多年来他一直对旧日对手怀恨在心。
senses.why: When the wish to harm settles and lasts, it hardens into resentment held against a person.
senses.whyCN: 当伤害的念头沉淀下来并持续，它就硬化为对某个人怀有的怨恨。

senses.title: Injurious words or acts
senses.titleCN: 恶语的伤害：言语或行为的伤人意图
senses.definition: the harm that an intention to injure can bring through words or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 伤人的意图通过言语或对待方式造成的伤害
senses.example: The court found malice in the way the story was published.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭在报道刊发的方式中认定存在恶意。
senses.why: The inner badness leaks out into words and treatment, so malice can also name the injury an intention produces.
senses.whyCN: 内心的坏从言语与对待方式里渗出来，所以 malice 也能指这种意图造成的伤害。

senses.title: Covert ill will
senses.definition: an unspoken ill will that shows only in hints, looks or small acts
senses.definitionCN: 不明说、只从暗示、眼神或小动作中露出的不良用心
senses.example: There was malice in his polite smile.
senses.exampleCN: 他那礼貌的微笑里透着恶意。
senses.why: Because the word names what is hidden, it often describes ill will that polite surfaces try to cover.
senses.whyCN: 正因为这个词指隐藏的东西，它常用来描述被礼貌表面掩盖住的不良用心。

intro.en: Malice comes from Latin malitia, badness, from malus, bad, through Old French malice.
intro.cn: malice 来自拉丁语 malitia（坏、恶），源于 malus（坏的），经古法语 malice 进入英语。

items.en: Malus means bad or evil, and malitia means badness or mischievousness.
items.cn: 拉丁语 malus 意为「坏的、邪恶的」，malitia 意为「坏、恶行」。

items.en: Some Latin glosses use malitia for wickedness of the heart as well as for bad quality.
items.cn: 部分拉丁语注释中，malitia 既指品质之坏，也指内心的邪恶。

items.en: Malice carries the meaning into Old French.
items.cn: malice 把这个含义带入古法语。

items.en: Malice enters English from around the thirteenth century with the sense of wickedness and ill will.
items.cn: 约十三世纪起，malice 以「邪恶、不良用心」的意思进入英语。

items.en: Law fixes the word in phrases such as malice aforethought, so intention becomes a legal fact.
items.cn: 法律把它固定在 malice aforethought 一类短语中，使「意图」成为法律事实。

items.en: Everyday English softens it into a mere wish to hurt, as in with malice.
items.cn: 现代英语把它软化，只表示「想伤害」的念头，见搭配 with malice。

note.en: Malice belongs to the malus family with malicious, malign and malignant, and sits near spite, hatred and hostility in meaning.
note.cn: malice 与 malicious、malign、malignant 同属 malus 词族，在意义上与 spite、hatred、hostility 相邻。

entries.definition: showing a wish to hurt others
evil in nature, or to speak ill of someone
entries.definitionCN: 恶毒的；诽谤，与 malice 词源相邻

entries.definition: very harmful, and in medicine growing out of control
entries.definitionCN: 恶性的；医学上指失控生长的，本义「怀有恶意」

entries.definition: a wish to annoy or hurt someone, often because of being wronged
entries.definitionCN: 恶意；怨恨，常因自感受委屈而起

entries.definition: a very strong feeling of dislike
entries.definitionCN: 憎恨；仇恨，比 malice 更具情绪性

entries.definition: the wish to do evil to others
entries.definitionCN: 恶毒之心，最贴近 malice 的正式名词

normalIntro.en: Malice keeps the Latin stem for bad, so its relatives all point back to the same root.
normalIntro.cn: malice 保留了拉丁语中表示「坏」的词干，它的同族词都指回同一词根。

normal.en: Latin malitia comes from malus, bad, the same stem as malformation.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 malitia 源于 malus（坏的），与 malformation 共用同一词干。

normal.en: The adjective malicious adds -ious, and maliciously adds -ly on top.
normal.cn: 形容词 malicious 加上了 -ious，maliciously 又在其上加 -ly。

normal.en: The phrase with malice marks an act done on purpose.
normal.cn: 搭配 with malice 标记一个有意的行为。

normal.en: Bearing malice means holding a grudge, so the word often sits with bear.
normal.cn: bear malice 表示怀恨，因此这个词常与动词 bear 连用。

normal.en: Legal use keeps malice aforethought, meaning a plan to kill formed before the act.
normal.cn: 法律用法保留 malice aforethought，指行为之前就形成的杀人预谋。

abstract.en: Picture a knife wrapped in a silk napkin: the surface is polite, the blade is ready.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀被丝巾裹着：表面客气，刀锋却已备好。

abstract.en: See a legal file stamped with a word that proves the accused meant to hurt.
abstract.cn: 想象一份法律卷宗上盖着一枚字印，证明被告本来就打算伤人。

abstract.en: Imagine a grudge carried in a pocket for years, growing heavier each time it is taken out.
abstract.cn: 想象一份怨恨被揣在口袋里多年，每次翻看就变得更沉。

examples.en: There was no malice in her remarks, only honesty.
examples.cn: 她的话里没有恶意，只是坦率。

examples.en: The lawyer must prove malice to win the libel case.
examples.cn: 律师必须证明存在恶意才能打赢这场诽谤官司。

examples.en: He took the job out of malice, not out of interest.
examples.cn: 他接这份工作是出于恶意，而不是出于兴趣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「骂你死」——嘴边骂着你，心里想着你死，正是恶意；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 malus（坏的、邪恶的）→ malitia（坏、恶）→ 古法语 malice → 英语 malice，核心义「心里的坏」。同族词有 malicious、malign、malignant。

sensesIntro.en: Malice begins as a wish to hurt, becomes a legal intention, hardens into resentment, leaks into injurious words, and finally hides under politeness.
sensesIntro.cn: malice 起初是伤人的念头，随后成为法律上的故意，再硬化为怨恨，渗进伤人的言语，最后藏进礼貌的表面之下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a polite smile with a hidden blade behind it, aimed at someone the speaker has decided to hurt.
core.cn: 核心意象：礼貌的微笑背后藏着一把刀，指向说话者已决定要伤害的人。

branches.en: The inner line: the wish to hurt is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 内心线：想伤害他人的念头是最日常的义项。

branches.en: The legal line: the wish becomes provable intent in court.
branches.cn: 法律线：念头在法庭上变成可证明的意图。

branches.en: The grudge line: a lasting resentment keeps the wish alive for years.
branches.cn: 怨恨线：持久的怨恨让这念头经年不散。

branches.en: The action line: intent becomes words and treatment that injure.
branches.cn: 行动线：意图变成伤人的言语与对待方式。

branches.en: The hidden line: what is hidden behind courtesy is the quiet version of the same wish.
branches.cn: 隐藏线：藏在客气背后的，正是同一种念头的安静版本。

intro.en: Malice is the Latin stem for bad plus the ordinary noun ending, and English builds malicious, maliciously and the legal phrases around it.
intro.cn: malice 是拉丁语表「坏」的词干加普通名词词尾，英语围绕它构成 malicious、maliciously 以及法律短语。

latinIntro.en: Latin malus means bad, and malitia means badness or wickedness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 malus 意为「坏的」，malitia 意为「坏、邪恶」。

items.example: The prefix mal- marks something as bad.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mal- 把某物标为「坏」。

items.example: Malus is the adjective behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: malus 是整个词族背后的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -itia turns the adjective into malitia.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -itia 把形容词变成 malitia。

items.meaningCN: 性质或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -ice forms malice from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ice 让拉丁词干成为 malice。

items.example: The suffix -ious forms malicious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ious 构成 malicious。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms maliciously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 maliciously。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms malignant from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 用同一词干构成 malignant。

items.example: Malicious describes a person or an act.
items.exampleCN: malicious 形容人或行为。

items.example: Malevolent uses the same bad prefix with a Latin wishing root.
items.exampleCN: malevolent 用同一个坏前缀配拉丁语「意愿」词根。

definition_zh: 可锻的；有延展性的；易受影响的；善于适应的；可塑的
definition_en: able to be hammered or pressed into shape without breaking, and figuratively easy to influence or adapt
core_image: 铁匠锤子落下，金属被压成薄片却始终不断裂，还能继续改变形状
scene: 铁匠铺里，红热的铁块在锤子下一点点摊开，始终不裂，能被敲成任何形状。In the forge the red hot bar stayed malleable under the hammer and could be shaped into a thin blade.
sceneCN: 这里 malleable 是「可锻的」（第 1 个义项：金属受锤压后能变形而不裂、仍可继续塑形的性质）；句意为铁料在锤打下一直保持可锻状态，最后被敲成一片薄刃。

pos.zh: 可锻的；有延展性的；易受人影响的；可塑的

collocations.zh: 高度可塑的；极易受影响的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可锻性；延展性；可塑性」
形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可塑地；顺从地」
同源动词，义为「用锤子锻打；轧制」
同源名词，义为「木槌；锤」，与拉丁语「锤」的词源相关

senses.title: A metal that can be worked
senses.titleCN: 可锻的：能受锤压变形而不裂的金属
senses.definition: describes a metal that can be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without cracking
senses.definitionCN: 形容金属能被锤打或轧成薄片而不会开裂
senses.example: Gold is so malleable that a gram can cover a large sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 黄金的可锻性极强，一克就能压成一大片金箔。
senses.why: The Latin root is the word for a hammer, so the adjective first names the metal that yields to the hammer instead of breaking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根意为「锤子」，所以这个形容词最初命名的是那种会顺从锤子而不是断裂的金属。

senses.title: A material that can be shaped
senses.titleCN: 可塑的：材料能被任意塑形
senses.definition: describes any solid material that can be pressed or rolled into a new shape
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何固体材料能被压扁或轧成新的形状
senses.example: The clay is malleable while it stays wet.
senses.exampleCN: 黏土在保持湿润时是可塑的。
senses.why: The hammer steps back and the idea of yielding to pressure widens to clay, wax and warmed plastic.
senses.whyCN: 锤子退居幕后，「受压力而变形」这层意思扩展到黏土、蜡与加热后的塑料。

senses.title: A mind that is easy to mould
senses.titleCN: 易受影响的：心智容易被塑造
senses.definition: describes a person or mind that is easily influenced, trained or changed by others
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或心智容易被他人影响、训练或改变
senses.example: Children are most malleable in their early years.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童在早年最容易受影响。
senses.why: Bendable metal becomes a metaphor for a mind that takes the shape someone else presses into it.
senses.whyCN: 可弯折的金属成为隐喻，指一种会照着别人压出的形状成型的头脑。

senses.title: A system open to change
senses.titleCN: 易调整的：制度或计划可灵活改动
senses.definition: describes a plan, system or arrangement that can easily be adapted
senses.definitionCN: 形容计划、制度或安排容易被调整
senses.example: The schedule is malleable enough to absorb late changes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份日程足够灵活，可以容纳临时改动。
senses.why: Anything with a set shape, from metal to a timetable, can be called malleable when it keeps yielding.
senses.whyCN: 任何已有形状的东西，从金属到时间表，只要还能继续让步，都可以称作可塑。

senses.title: A record that can be altered
senses.titleCN: 可被改写的：数据或记忆易被篡改
senses.definition: describes data, memory or evidence that can be rewritten or tampered with
senses.definitionCN: 形容数据、记忆或证据可以被改写或篡改
senses.example: Paper records are malleable and easy to misplace.
senses.exampleCN: 纸质记录容易被改动，也容易丢失。
senses.why: In computing and psychology the metaphor turns negative: a malleable record keeps no firm shape of its own.
senses.whyCN: 在计算机与心理学中，这个隐喻转向负面：可改写的记录自身没有固定形状。

senses.title: A person easy to persuade
senses.titleCN: 好说话的：容易被说服的人
senses.definition: describes a person who tends to agree with others too easily
senses.definitionCN: 形容人太容易顺着他人的意见
senses.example: He is too malleable to refuse the manager a second time.
senses.exampleCN: 他太好说话，第二次也没法拒绝经理。
senses.why: The talk of yielding to pressure turns social, so a malleable person is one who bends rather than holds a line.
senses.whyCN: 「受压而让步」的说法转向社会层面，好说话的人就是会弯下去而守不住底线的人。

intro.en: Malleable comes from medieval Latin malleabilis, which goes back to malleare, to hammer, and ultimately to malleus, a hammer.
intro.cn: malleable 来自中世纪拉丁语 malleabilis，再追溯到 malleare（锤打）与 malleus（锤子）。

items.en: Malleus means a hammer, and malleare means to hammer.
items.cn: 拉丁语 malleus 意为「锤子」，malleare 意为「锤打」。

items.en: Malleabilis, hammerable, is built from the verb with the adjective suffix.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 malleabilis（可被锤打的）由动词加形容词后缀构成。

items.en: English takes the adjective in the fourteenth century, probably through French or directly from Latin.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收这个形容词，来源可能是法语，也可能直接取自拉丁语。

items.en: Early use is technical and metallurgical, applying to metal that can be beaten flat.
items.cn: 早期用法是技术与冶金上的，指能被敲平的金属。

items.en: Later writers extend the adjective to temper, mind and character.
items.cn: 后来的作者把这一形容词扩展到性情、心智与性格。

items.en: Physics, computing and psychology now use it for anything that can be reshaped.
items.cn: 如今物理、计算机与心理学用它指任何可被重塑之物。

note.en: Malleable shares the Latin hammer with mallet and malleate, and in meaning it neighbours ductile, pliable and flexible.
note.cn: malleable 与 mallet、malleate 共享拉丁语「锤子」，在意义上与 ductile、pliable、flexible 相邻。

entries.definition: the quality of being malleable
a wooden hammer
entries.definitionCN: 木槌；锤，共享拉丁语「锤子」词源

entries.definition: to hammer into thin sheets
able to be drawn out into wire
entries.definitionCN: 可拉成丝的；韧性的，与可锻侧重不同

entries.definition: easy to bend without breaking
entries.definitionCN: 易弯的；柔软的，也指人顺从

entries.definition: able to bend or change easily

normalIntro.en: Malleable is built on the Latin word for a hammer, so the hammer is the key to the whole family.
normalIntro.cn: malleable 建立在拉丁语「锤子」一词上，锤子是理解整个词族的关键。

normal.en: Latin malleus means hammer, and malleare means to hammer.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 malleus 意为锤子，malleare 意为锤打。

normal.en: The suffix -able means able to be, so malleable means able to be hammered.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 表示「可以被……」，所以 malleable 就是「可以被锤打的」。

normal.en: The suffix -ity builds the noun malleability.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ity 构成名词 malleability。

normal.en: The noun mallet keeps the hammer meaning in ordinary life.
normal.cn: 名词 mallet 在日常生活中保留了「锤子」的意思。

normal.en: In metallurgy malleable contrasts with brittle: one bends, the other cracks.
normal.cn: 在冶金学里 malleable 与 brittle 相对：一个弯得下去，一个会折断。

abstract.en: Picture a goldsmith beating a coin into a sheet thinner than paper without cracking it.
abstract.cn: 想象金匠把一枚金币敲成比纸还薄的薄片，却没有把它敲裂。

abstract.en: Imagine a lump of clay that takes the print of any thumb that presses it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块黏土，谁的拇指按下去就印出谁的指纹。

abstract.en: See a young mind like soft wax that takes the shape of whatever it is pressed into.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗年轻的心像软蜡，被按进什么模子就成什么形状。

examples.en: Copper is malleable enough to be beaten into thin sheets.
examples.cn: 铜的可锻性足以被敲成薄片。

examples.en: Teenagers are still malleable enough to change their habits.
examples.cn: 青少年的可塑性还很强，足以改变习惯。

examples.en: The software keeps its data in a malleable form that anyone can edit.
examples.cn: 这个软件以可随意改写的格式保存数据，任何人都能编辑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马丽儿」——锤子一捶，铁片像她手里的软糖一样摊开：可锻的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 malleus（锤子）→ malleare（锤打）→ 中世纪拉丁语 malleabilis（可被锤打的）→ 英语 malleable，核心义「受锤压而变形不坏」。同族词有 mallet、malleate、malleability。

sensesIntro.en: Malleable starts with metal that takes the hammer, widens to any material that yields, and then moves to minds, systems, records and people that others can reshape.
sensesIntro.cn: malleable 从顺从锤子的金属开始，扩展到任何受压变形的材料，再转向可被他人重塑的心智、制度、记录与人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hammer falls on hot metal, which flattens into a new shape instead of cracking.
core.cn: 核心意象：锤子落在红热的金属上，金属被压成新的形状而没有碎裂。

branches.en: The metallurgy line: the hammerable metal is the literal core.
branches.cn: 冶金线：可被锤打的金属是最字面的核心。

branches.en: The material line: yielding to pressure spreads from metal to clay and wax.
branches.cn: 材料线：受压让步从金属扩展到黏土与蜡。

branches.en: The people line: a mind or a person takes the shape others press into them.
branches.cn: 人物线：心智或人本身会照着别人压出的形状成型。

branches.en: The system line: plans and schedules stay shapeless enough to absorb change.
branches.cn: 制度线：计划与日程没有固定死形状，因而能吸收变化。

branches.en: The record line: data keeps no firm shape and can be rewritten.
branches.cn: 记录线：数据没有固定形状，因而可被改写。

intro.en: Malleable is the Latin hammer root plus the English suffix -able, and English builds malleability, malleate and the related noun mallet on the same stem.
intro.cn: malleable 是拉丁语「锤子」词根加英语后缀 -able，英语又在同一词干上构成 malleability、malleate 以及相关的名词 mallet。

latinIntro.en: Latin malleus means hammer, and malleare means to hammer, so the adjective names what can be hammered.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 malleus 意为锤子，malleare 意为锤打，因此这个形容词命名的是「可被锤打的东西」。

items.example: The root malle- supplies the hammer image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 malle- 提供「锤子」的意象。

items.example: Malleus is the direct source of the root.
items.exampleCN: malleus 是这一词根的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -able makes the verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把动词变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms malleability.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 malleability。

items.meaning: able to be hammered into shape
items.example: Malleable keeps both the metal and the mind sense.
items.exampleCN: malleable 兼指金属与心智。

items.example: Malleability is the noun of the quality.
items.exampleCN: malleability 是表示这种性质的名词。

items.example: Malleate is the technical verb of hammering.
items.exampleCN: malleate 是表示锤打的技术动词。

items.example: Mallet keeps the hammer in the toolbox.
items.exampleCN: mallet 把锤子留在了工具箱里。

items.example: Malleolar comes from a different small hammer shaped bone.
items.exampleCN: malleolar 源自另一块形似小锤的骨头。

definition_zh: 麦芽；麦芽酒；淡啤酒；威士忌；使发芽制成麦芽
definition_en: grain, especially barley, that has been soaked and partly sprouted for brewing; also the drink or spirit made from it
core_image: 金黄的大麦粒在湿木桶里泡胀，探出一点白白嫩芽
scene: 旧厂房的木地板上，泡过水的谷物铺成薄薄一层，正冒出细白的芽。Malt lies in a thin layer on the floor of an old factory, its white shoots just breaking out.
sceneCN: 这里 malt 是「麦芽」（第 1 个义项：发芽后烘干的谷物）；句意：麦芽薄薄一层铺在旧厂房的地板上，白色嫩芽刚刚冒出。

pos.zh: 麦芽；（由麦芽酿的）麦芽酒、啤酒、威士忌

derivatives.zh: 由动词 malt 加 -ed 构成，义为「制成麦芽的；含麦芽的」，如 malted milk 麦乳精
由动词 malt 加 -ing 构成，义为「制麦芽；麦芽制作」，是酿酒业的一道工序
由 malt 加古英语施事后缀 -ster 构成，义为「制麦芽的人；制麦芽工」
由 malt 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「带麦芽味的；麦芽香的」

senses.title: Sprouted grain used for brewing
senses.definition: grain, usually barley, that has been soaked and allowed to sprout, then dried, for use in brewing or distilling
senses.definitionCN: 通常指大麦等谷物，经浸泡促其发芽后再烘干，用于酿造或蒸馏
senses.example: The malt is dried slowly so that its natural sweetness stays in the grain.
senses.exampleCN: 麦芽要慢慢烘干，好让天然的甜味留在谷物里。
senses.why: The Old English form probably meant something soft or dissolved; steeped grain becomes soft and swelling, so the word settled on the softened, sprouting grain itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式很可能本指「柔软、被泡开」的东西；泡过的谷物变得发软发胀，于是这个词落到「泡软、已发芽的谷物」这个核心意象上。

senses.title: Ale or beer brewed from malt
senses.definition: a drink, especially ale or beer, made by brewing malted grain
senses.definitionCN: 用麦芽酿造而成的饮料，尤指麦芽酒、啤酒
senses.example: "Two glasses of malt, please," the traveller said as he sat down by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 「请来两杯麦芽酒。」旅人在炉火边坐下时说道。
senses.why: Once the grain is the main ingredient, the name of the ingredient spreads to the drink it produces.
senses.whyCN: 一旦谷物成了主要原料，表示原料的名称就顺势延伸到它酿出的饮料，这是很常见的一类转指。

senses.title: A beer of this kind
senses.definition: any of various pale or amber beers associated with malt brewing, as in bottled or canned malt
senses.definitionCN: 与麦芽酿造有关的各类浅色或琥珀色啤酒，如瓶装或罐装的麦芽啤酒
senses.example: The shop sells stout, lager and a sweet dark malt in tall bottles.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售世涛、拉格啤酒，还有大瓶装的甜味深色麦芽啤。
senses.why: In shops and menus the drink sense narrows again into a label for particular malt flavoured beers.
senses.whyCN: 在商店货架和菜单上，「饮料」这一义项又进一步收窄，专门给某类麦芽味啤酒当品名，所以从中分出一个义项。

senses.title: Whisky made from malted barley
senses.definition: a whisky distilled from malted barley, especially one produced in Scotland
senses.definitionCN: 用发芽大麦蒸馏而成的威士忌，尤指苏格兰出产的
senses.example: He ordered a single malt and watched the amber liquid settle.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯单一麦芽威士忌，看着琥珀色的酒液渐渐安定下来。
senses.why: Distillation keeps the same ingredient name; a single malt means one distillery using only malted barley.
senses.whyCN: 蒸馏工艺同样以原料命名；所谓单一麦芽，是指只用发芽大麦、出自同一家酒厂的酒，因此威士忌也从这层原料意象里长出来。

senses.title: Malt flavour or malt extract
senses.definition: a taste or extract that recalls malt, used in milk, biscuits, syrup and vinegar
senses.definitionCN: 近似麦芽的味道或提取物，用于调奶、饼干、糖浆和醋
senses.example: Malted milk powder gives the shake a warm malt flavour.
senses.exampleCN: 麦乳精粉让这杯奶昔带上一股温润的麦芽味。
senses.why: The grain leaves a sweet, toasted note behind, so food makers use the word for that flavour and for the extract that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 谷物会留下一股甜香微焦的味道，食品商因此用这个词指那种风味，也指承载风味的提取物。

senses.title: To make grain into malt
senses.definition: to steep, sprout and dry grain so that it becomes malt
senses.definitionCN: 把谷物浸泡、催芽并烘干，使其成为麦芽
senses.example: The brewers malt their own barley in the old stone floor maltings.
senses.exampleCN: 酿酒师在旧式石板麦芽车间里自己把大麦制成麦芽。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb when brewing became an industrial process someone performs on the grain.
senses.whyCN: 当酿造变成一道可以对谷物加工实施的工序时，名词就转成了动词，表示「把谷物做成麦芽」。

senses.title: Grain steeping and sprouting as a process
senses.definition: the stage in brewing in which grain is steeped and germinated before roasting
senses.definitionCN: 酿造中谷物在烘烤前进行浸泡与发芽的阶段
senses.example: During malting, enzymes wake up and soften the starch inside each grain.
senses.exampleCN: 在制麦过程中，酶被激活，使每粒谷物里的淀粉变得松软。
senses.why: In malting jargon the same ingredient name also names the whole step that turns grain into the ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 在制麦行业里，同一个原料名称又延伸为「把谷物变成麦芽」的整个工序，因为这道工序产出的就是它本身。

senses.title: Malt as shorthand for a tall glass
senses.definition: a glass or serving of a malt drink, chiefly in North American informal use
senses.definitionCN: 一杯或一份麦芽饮料，主要用于北美口语
senses.example: He came in from the cold and asked for a hot malt.
senses.exampleCN: 他从寒风中进来，要了一杯热麦芽饮。
senses.why: Like many drink words, it can stand for one measure of the drink, so a malt can simply mean a glass of it.
senses.whyCN: 和许多饮料词一样，它可以指「一份」饮料，所以 a malt 在口语里就简单表示一杯麦芽饮，与核心的「麦芽」意象只隔一层。

intro.en: Malt is recorded in Old English as mealt, and the spelling malt appears in Middle English; the deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: malt 在古英语中写作 mealt，中古英语中出现 malt 这一拼写；更深一层的来源尚不确定。

items.en: The word goes back to a Germanic noun reconstructed as maltaz; coinage of the noun in ancient times is probable, the exact root is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词可追溯到重构的日耳曼语名词 maltaz；该名词在古代即已造出，但确切词根来源不确定。

items.en: Mealt appears in Old English, naming grain prepared for brewing.
items.cn: 古英语 mealt 已经出现，指为酿造而处理过的谷物。

items.en: Old Norse malt shows the same word in the neighbouring Germanic speech.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 malt 显示同一地区相邻的日耳曼语言里也有这个词。

items.en: Middle English malt is used for the brewing grain and for the drink made from it.
items.cn: 中古英语 malt 兼指酿造用的谷物与用它酿出的饮料。

items.en: Malt becomes a factory process, and maltings and maltsters appear.
items.cn: 制麦逐渐成为工厂化的工序，出现了 maltings 与 maltsters。

items.en: Single malt whisky, malted milk and malt extract extend the word to spirits and foods.
items.cn: 单一麦芽威士忌、麦乳精与麦精把词义扩展到烈酒和食品领域。

note.en: Malt sits in a brewing family with barley, hops, ale and whisky, and is close in spelling to malted and melting.
note.cn: malt 处在酿造词语家族中，与 barley、hops、ale、whisky 相邻，拼写上又容易与 malted、melting 混淆。

entries.definition: made into or flavoured with malt
entries.definitionCN: 制成麦芽的；加了麦芽的

entries.definition: the making of malt, or a place where grain is malted
tasting of malt
to turn from solid to liquid
entries.definitionCN: 融化；只是拼写和发音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a tall cereal grass used as food and in brewing
the flowers used to flavour and preserve beer
entries.definitionCN: 啤酒花；给啤酒调味并防腐

entries.definition: unfermented liquid drawn from mashed malt
entries.definitionCN: 麦芽汁；从麦芽糖化液中滤出的液体

entries.definition: a pale beer brewed without hops in older times

normalIntro.en: Malt is soaked grain in its first green push: the grain is soft, swollen and just sprouting.
normalIntro.cn: malt 是被泡胀、刚要冒芽的谷物：颗粒发软、发胀，带着一点白芽。

normal.en: Single malt is whisky from one distillery using only malted barley.
normal.cn: single malt 指同一家酒厂只用发芽大麦酿出的威士忌。

normal.en: A maltster is the person who makes malt; the -ster names the trade.
normal.cn: maltster 是制麦芽的人，词尾 -ster 表示从事某行当的人。

normal.en: Malt vinegar and malt extract keep the word as an ingredient label.
normal.cn: malt vinegar 与 malt extract 把词保留在原料名称的用法里。

normal.en: Malted milk is milk powder plus malt extract, a sweet drink.
normal.cn: malted milk 是奶粉加麦精，一种甜饮。

normal.en: As a verb, to malt grain is to steep, sprout and dry it.
normal.cn: 作动词时，to malt grain 指把谷物浸泡、发芽再烘干。

abstract.en: Picture warm wet barley swelling, each grain with a tiny white root.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖潮湿的大麦泡胀，每粒都钻出小小的白根。

abstract.en: See a barrel tapping beer as dark as amber.
abstract.cn: 想象木桶里流出琥珀色的啤酒。

abstract.en: Think of a bottle labeled with one distillery and a capital letter.
abstract.cn: 想到一只只标着一家酒厂名字的威士忌酒瓶。

examples.en: The distillery soaks its barley in cold water before leaving it to malt.
examples.cn: 这家酒厂先把大麦泡进冷水，再让它发芽成为麦芽。

examples.en: Malt gives the beer its colour and much of its sweetness.
examples.cn: 麦芽赋予啤酒色泽和大部分甜味。

examples.en: He prefers a light malt to a strong spirit.
examples.cn: 比起烈酒，他更喜欢清淡的麦芽啤酒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦」尔特的汤——把大麦泡成一锅「麦」芽汤；麦芽读音近去声，念起来就像麦子发了芽。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为可追溯至日耳曼语重构形式 maltaz（泡软的谷物），古英语作 mealt，中古英语作 malt；更深层词根来源不确定。核心义「泡软、发芽的谷物」，后扩展为用它酿的饮料、烈酒与风味。

sensesIntro.en: Malt starts as sprouted brewing grain, spreads to the drinks made from it, and then to whisky, flavourings and the brewing process itself.
sensesIntro.cn: malt 起于发芽的酿酒谷物，延伸到用它酿的饮料，再扩散到威士忌、风味提取物以及制麦工序本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soaked barley swelling in a wet wooden vat, a white shoot breaking through.
core.cn: 核心意象：泡在湿木桶里的大麦粒胀开，冒出一点白芽。

branches.en: The sprouted grain itself is the core sense.
branches.cn: 发芽的谷物本身是核心义项。

branches.en: Ale and commercial malt beers are the drink made from the grain.
branches.cn: 麦芽酒与市售麦芽啤酒是谷物酿出的饮料。

branches.en: Whisky carries the ingredient name into the distilled spirit.
branches.cn: 威士忌把这层原料名称带进了蒸馏烈酒。

branches.en: Malt flavour and extract keep only the taste of the grain.
branches.cn: 麦芽味与麦精只保留了谷物的味道。

branches.en: The noun becomes a verb and a process name for making the grain.
branches.cn: 名词变成动词和工序名称，表示制作麦芽。

intro.en: Malt is a Germanic base word rather than a Latinate construction, and its family grows with the English suffixes -ed, -ing, -ster and -y.
intro.cn: malt 是日耳曼语系的根词，不是拉丁语构词，它的词族靠英语后缀 -ed、-ing、-ster 与 -y 生长开来。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestry, so the entries here are English forms built on the Germanic base.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语渊源，这里列出的是在日耳曼词根上构成的英语形式。

items.meaningCN: 麦芽；酿酒用的发芽谷物
items.example: Malt is the base of most beer.
items.exampleCN: 麦芽是大多数啤酒的基础。

items.example: They malt barley on the old floor.
items.exampleCN: 他们在旧车间里把大麦制成麦芽。

items.meaning: more than one malt; he or it malts
items.meaningCN: 麦芽的复数；第三人称单数动词
items.example: The bar serves several malts.
items.exampleCN: 这家酒吧供应好几种麦芽酒。

items.meaningCN: 用麦芽做的；加了麦芽的
items.example: Malted milk is a sweet drink.
items.exampleCN: 麦乳精是一种甜饮。

items.meaning: the process or buildings for making malt
items.example: Malting wakes up enzymes in the grain.
items.exampleCN: 制麦过程会让谷物里的酶活跃起来。

items.meaningCN: 表示某种职业或从业者的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ster forms maltster.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ster 构成 maltster。

items.example: The maltster checked the grain each night.
items.exampleCN: 制麦芽工每晚都查看谷物。

items.example: The suffix -y forms malty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 malty。

items.example: The stout is rich and malty.
items.exampleCN: 这款世涛浓郁带麦芽香。

items.example: A single malt comes from one distillery.
items.exampleCN: 单一麦芽威士忌出自同一家酒厂。

definition_en: to treat a person or animal cruelly or roughly
core_image: 一双手本该轻轻托住，却重重地按下去
scene: 动物收容所里，那只瘦狗见到人抬手的动作就往后缩，显然曾被粗暴对待。At the shelter the thin dog flinched when a hand was raised, as if it had been maltreated before.
sceneCN: 这里 maltreat 是「虐待、粗暴对待」（第 1 个义项：残忍或粗暴地对待人或动物）；句意：收容所里那只瘦狗一见人抬手就往后缩，好像以前被虐待过。

derivatives.zh: 由 maltreat 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「虐待；粗暴对待」，是法律与医学文件中常见的正式说法
由 maltreat 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「施虐者」，较少使用，多作法律或新闻用语
由 mis-（错误、不当）加 treat 构成，义为「虐待；不公正对待」，与 maltreat 近义但更通用
由 ill（恶劣地）加 treat 构成，义为「虐待」，尤其常见于旧式英式英语

senses.title: To treat a person or animal cruelly
senses.definition: to treat someone, especially a person or an animal, cruelly, roughly or unjustly
senses.definitionCN: 残忍、粗暴或不公正地对待某人，尤指人或动物
senses.example: The farmer was fined for maltreating the horses in his care.
senses.exampleCN: 那名农场主因虐待自己照管的马而被罚款。
senses.why: The prefix mal- carries the Latin sense of badly, so maltreat is simply a treating that is done badly, and the core image is a hand that should support but presses down instead.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 mal- 带着拉丁语「坏地、恶地」的意思，所以 maltreat 字面上就是「把对待搞坏」；核心意象是一只本该托住对方的手反而重重按下去，义项就由此而来。

senses.title: To use something roughly
senses.definition: to handle a thing badly, roughly or carelessly, so that it looks worn or spoiled
senses.definitionCN: 对待物品时粗暴或漫不经心，使其显得磨损或被糟蹋
senses.example: The suitcase had been maltreated by three airports and lost a wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 那只行李箱被三家机场摔来摔去，丢了一个轮子。
senses.why: Because any treatment can be bad treatment, the verb also spreads from living creatures to things that get handled badly.
senses.whyCN: 既然「对待」的对象不限于生命，只要处理得不好就能叫坏对待，所以义项从人畜扩散到被粗暴摆弄的物品。

senses.title: To treat the language or text carelessly
senses.definition: to damage or misuse a language, a text or an argument by careless handling
senses.definitionCN: 因粗心处理而损害、滥用语言、文本或论据
senses.example: Critics said the translator had maltreated the original poetry.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称那位译者糟改了原诗。
senses.why: The pattern of treating badly applies to anything with a proper way of being handled, including a text or a language.
senses.whyCN: 凡是本有正确处理方式的对象都能套进「坏对待」的框架，文本和语言也不例外，于是出现了这一较文的义项。

senses.title: To keep someone in harsh conditions
senses.definition: to keep someone in overcrowded, underfed or unsafe conditions as a continuing pattern of ill treatment
senses.definitionCN: 长期使某人处于拥挤、缺乏食物或不安全的环境中，构成持续性的苛待
senses.example: Reports said the detainees were being maltreated in crowded cells.
senses.exampleCN: 有报告称被拘留者在拥挤的牢房里备受虐待。
senses.why: Ill treatment often takes the form of conditions rather than a single blow, so the verb covers ongoing harsh custody.
senses.whyCN: 虐待往往不是一下重手，而是日复一日的恶劣条件；因此这个动词也能指长期的严苛羁押。

senses.title: Maltreated as an adjective participle
senses.definition: used as a participle adjective for a person, an animal or a thing that has a history of being badly treated
senses.definitionCN: 作分词形容词，指人或动物、物品有过被苛待的经历
senses.example: The rescue group finds homes for maltreated dogs every weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个救助组织每个周末都为受虐的狗寻找领养家庭。
senses.why: Once a treatment is completed, its result stays with the receiver, so the past participle works as an adjective of lasting condition.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对待发生完，结果就留在承受者身上，所以过去分词可以当形容词用，表示某种持续下来的状态。

intro.en: Maltreat is built from Latin mal-, badly, and tractare, to handle; it is a compound learned from French and Latin models rather than a single inherited word.
intro.cn: maltreat 由拉丁语前缀 mal-（坏地）与 tractare（处置、处理）构成，经古法语和拉丁语学术渠道进入英语。

items.en: Mal- comes from Latin malus, bad, and adds the sense of badly or wrongly to a base.
items.cn: mal- 来自拉丁语 malus（坏的），给词根加上「坏地、错误地」的意思。

items.en: Tractare means to handle, manage or deal with, formed from trahere, to draw.
items.cn: tractare 意为处理、对待，是 trahere（拉、牵）的反复动词。

items.en: Mal with traitier yields French maltraiter, to handle roughly or use someone badly.
items.cn: mal 与 traitier 组合成法语 maltraiter，意为粗暴对待、错待。

items.en: Maltreat enters English in the general sense of treating badly, and the noun maltreatment follows.
items.cn: maltreat 进入英语，最初就是一般意义上的「坏待」，并由此衍生出名词形式。

items.en: Church reports and legal documents spread maltreat and maltreatment to children, prisoners and animals.
items.cn: 教会报告与法律文件把 maltreat 与 maltreatment 推广到儿童、囚犯和动物话题上。

note.en: Maltreat is the formal verb of treating badly; its near kin are mis-, the Latin root tractare, and the everyday word abuse.
note.cn: maltreat 是表示「坏待」的正式动词，邻居包括前缀 mis-、拉丁词根 tractare，以及日常词 abuse。

entries.definition: to treat badly or unjustly
cruel or rough treatment
to behave towards someone or something
to move back or away
entries.definitionCN: 后退；撤退。只是拼写和发音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to treat a person or animal with cruelty or violence
to treat someone cruelly
to frighten or hurt someone weaker

normalIntro.en: Maltreat is mal plus treat: the same handling as a normal treat, only done badly and without care.
normalIntro.cn: maltreat 就是 mal 加 treat：本该是正常的对待，却被做坏、做得毫无关怀。

normal.en: The prefix mal- means badly, as in malformed and malfunction.
normal.cn: 前缀 mal- 表示坏地、不良地，如 malformed 与 malfunction。

normal.en: Treat shares its base with treatment and treaty; to treat someone is to deal with them.
normal.cn: treat 与 treatment、treaty 同源，都是「处理、对待」。

normal.en: Maltreatment is the noun common in law and social work.
normal.cn: maltreatment 是法律与社会工作中常用的名词形式。

normal.en: Mistreat, ill-treat and maltreat all mean treating badly, and maltreat is the most formal.
normal.cn: mistreat、ill-treat、maltreat 都表示坏待，其中 maltreat 最正式。

normal.en: Reports about animals, workers and prisoners often use the passive form be maltreated.
normal.cn: 被动结构 be maltreated 常见于关于动物、工人和囚犯的报道。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand raised to pat a dog, then slamming down instead.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手本想摸摸狗，却狠狠拍下去。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase thrown onto an airport belt again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱在传送带上一次又一次被摔来摔去。

abstract.en: See a report stamped with the short tag mal, marking a wrong deed.
abstract.cn: 想象一份报告上盖着 mal 两个字样的章，标出错误的行为。

examples.en: The inspector found that the calves had been maltreated for months.
examples.cn: 检查员发现这些牛犊已遭受数月虐待。

examples.en: It is a crime to maltreat an animal in this country.
examples.cn: 在这个国家，虐待动物是犯罪行为。

examples.en: She was determined not to maltreat the books she borrowed.
examples.cn: 她决心绝不糟蹋借来的书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「骂特」——一边骂、一边特别对待；被「骂特」了，就是被虐待。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mal-（坏的；坏地，源自 malus）+ tractare（处理、对待，源自 trahere 拉、牵）→ 中世纪法语 maltraiter（粗暴对待）→ 英语 maltreat「虐待、粗暴对待」。核心义「把对待搞坏」。

sensesIntro.en: Maltreat begins as cruelty to people or animals, then spreads to rough handling of things, careless use of language, harsh conditions and the participle adjective maltreated.
sensesIntro.cn: maltreat 先从对人畜的残忍开始，再扩散到对物品的粗暴摆弄、对语言文字的糟改、严苛的环境条件，以及分词形容词 maltreated。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that should hold up presses down hard.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该托住的手，反而重重地按下去。

branches.en: Cruelty to people or animals is the core sense.
branches.cn: 对人畜的残忍对待是核心义项。

branches.en: Rough handling of things extends the same pattern to objects.
branches.cn: 对物品的粗暴摆弄把同一模式延伸到物件上。

branches.en: Careless damage to a text or language is the literary extension.
branches.cn: 对文本或语言的糟改是书面语中的延伸。

branches.en: Ongoing harsh conditions are cruelty spread over time.
branches.cn: 持续性的恶劣条件是把虐待摊在时间上。

branches.en: Maltreated as an adjective keeps the result of the bad treatment.
branches.cn: maltreated 作形容词保留坏待留下的结果。

intro.en: Maltreat is a verb built on Latin parts: the prefix mal- adds the meaning badly to the verb treat, which derives from Latin tractare.
intro.cn: maltreat 是拉丁语构词：前缀 mal- 把「坏地」这一层意思加到 base treat 上，而 treat 来自拉丁语 tractare。

latinIntro.en: Latin malus means bad; tractare means to handle or deal with, and is the source of English treat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 malus 意为坏的，tractare 意为处理、对待，英语 treat 即由此而来。

items.example: The prefix mal- forms malformed.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mal- 构成 malformed。

items.example: Malus supplies the prefix mal-.
items.exampleCN: malus 提供了前缀 mal-。

items.example: Tractare gives the English treat.
items.exampleCN: tractare 演变出英语 treat。

items.example: Treat people as you wish to be treated.
items.exampleCN: 希望别人怎样待你，你就怎样待人。

items.example: Maltreat joins the two parts.
items.exampleCN: maltreat 把前后两部分合在一起。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作结果或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ment forms maltreatment.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成 maltreatment。

items.example: Maltreatment of children is a crime.
items.exampleCN: 虐待儿童是一种犯罪。

items.example: The suffix -er forms maltreater.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 maltreater。

items.example: Maltreater is rare but legal writers still use it.
items.exampleCN: maltreater 很少见，但法律写作中仍会使用。

items.example: The prefix mis- forms mistreat.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mis- 构成 mistreat。

items.example: The prefix ill- forms ill-treat.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ill- 构成 ill-treat。

definition_zh: 猛犸象；巨大的；庞大的；庞然大物
definition_en: a large extinct elephant with long curved tusks and thick hair; also extremely great in size, or a very large thing
core_image: 冰原上，一头长着螺旋长牙、披厚毛的巨象在雪雾中行走
scene: 博物馆展厅中央立着一头猛犸象的巨骨，弯曲的长牙几乎触到天花板。A mammoth skeleton stands in the museum hall, its curved tusks almost touching the ceiling.
sceneCN: 这里 mammoth 是「猛犸象」（第 1 个义项：冰期已灭绝的披毛巨象）；句意：展厅中央立着一副猛犸象骨架，弯曲的长牙几乎碰到天花板。

derivatives.zh: woolly（长毛的）加 mammoth 构成的复合名词，指冰期的「披毛猛犸象」，与 mammoth 同源同义，只是加上了外貌特征
由 mammoth 加 -like（像……的）构成，义为「像猛犸象一样巨大的」，常用于新闻写作
与 mammoth 只是拼写开头相近，来自拉丁语 mamma（乳房），义为「哺乳动物的」；两者词源不同，注意区分

senses.title: A huge extinct elephant
senses.definition: a very large extinct elephant of the Ice Age, with long curved tusks and a thick hairy coat
senses.definitionCN: 冰期生存的已灭绝巨型象类，长有弯曲长牙和厚毛
senses.example: A woolly mammoth could stand twice as tall as a modern elephant.
senses.exampleCN: 一头披毛猛犸象的身高可达现代大象的两倍。
senses.why: The word probably comes from a Siberian language and reached Russian as mammot; the animal itself is the original, literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能来自西伯利亚某语言，经俄语作 mammot；作为巨兽本身，这一义项是最早、最字面的用法。

senses.title: Extremely large in size
senses.definition: extremely large in size, amount or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在规模、数量或重要性上极其大
senses.example: The company faced a mammoth repair bill after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，公司面临一笔数额巨大的维修账单。
senses.why: The extinct elephant was proverbially enormous, so by the eighteenth century the noun had already become an adjective for anything huge.
senses.whyCN: 猛犸象以体型庞大著称，早在十八世纪名词就已转用作形容词，形容任何大得惊人的人或物，核心的「巨象尺度」因此延伸到抽象的大小。

senses.title: Very difficult and long
senses.definition: used of a task or effort whose scope is so vast that finishing it feels like a long hard climb
senses.definitionCN: 形容任务或努力的规模大到完成它像一场漫长艰难的攀登
senses.example: Cleaning up the river will be a mammoth task for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 清理这条河将是这座小镇一项艰巨浩大的任务。
senses.why: Size turns into effort when the huge thing is not a building but a job, so the adjective covers tasks as well as objects.
senses.whyCN: 当那个「巨大」的东西不是楼而是活计，尺度就变成了投入，所以形容词也用在任务上，表示艰巨浩大。

senses.title: Something enormous in shape
senses.definition: a thing of enormous size, especially a building, ship or vehicle that makes everything around it look small
senses.definitionCN: 体积极大的东西，尤指使周围一切都显得矮小的建筑、船或车辆
senses.example: The new library is a mammoth of glass and steel.
senses.exampleCN: 新图书馆是一座玻璃与钢铁的庞然大物。
senses.why: The noun keeps its shape sense by producing a new noun: a mammoth can be any oversized structure, not only a prehistoric beast.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留形状这一层，只是叉出一个新名词：mammoth 可以指任何超大结构，而不只是史前的巨兽，所以有了这个义项。

senses.title: Dated word for extremely
senses.definition: an old-fashioned intensifier meaning hugely or extremely, now rare
senses.definitionCN: 旧式程度加强词，意同「极其、巨大地」，今已罕见
senses.example: The Victorian newspaper called the new bridge mammoth expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 维多利亚时代的报纸称这座新桥造价高昂得惊人。
senses.why: Old journalism sharpened the adjective into an adverb of degree, a usage that has faded but survives in quotes.
senses.whyCN: 旧时新闻写作把形容词进一步锻造成程度副词，如今虽已退潮，仍在引语里留下痕迹。

intro.en: Mammoth reached English from Russian and was first recorded as the name of a Siberian beast; the ultimate Siberian origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: mammoth 经由俄语进入英语，最早记录为西伯利亚某巨兽的名字；更早的西伯利亚语来源不确定。

items.en: The original word is generally taken to come from a Siberian language, but the exact language and form are uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原词来自西伯利亚某语言，但具体是哪一种、原形如何，来源不确定。

items.en: Russian mammot or mamut names the huge bones and tusks found in the frozen ground.
items.cn: 俄语 mammot 或 mamut 指冻土中出土的巨大骨骼与长牙。

items.en: Early English travellers record mammoth as the name of a giant beast of Siberia.
items.cn: 十七世纪的英国旅行者把 mammoth 记为西伯利亚巨兽的名字。

items.en: The fossil elephant is identified, and mammoth starts to mean enormous in general.
items.cn: 现已认明化石属于象类，mammoth 也开始泛指「巨大」。

items.en: Mammoth settles as an adjective for tasks, sums and crowds, and as a noun for huge things.
items.cn: 十九世纪 mammoth 定型为形容词，用于任务、金额与人群，也作名词指庞然大物。

items.en: Dated specimens and permafrost finds refresh the literal sense beside the figurative one.
items.cn: 冻土中的发现与年代久远的标本，让字面义与比喻义在现代英语里并存。

note.en: Mammoth pairs the name of a prehistoric animal with the adjectives huge and enormous, and stands close to huge and giant in meaning.
note.cn: mammoth 既是一头史前动物的名字，又作 huge、enormous 一类的形容词，在义场上靠近 woolly 与 ivory。

entries.definition: covered with thick soft hair
entries.definitionCN: 长着厚软毛的；常见于 woolly mammoth 披毛猛犸象

entries.definition: of the group of animals that feed their young with milk
entries.definitionCN: 哺乳动物的。只是拼写开头相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a warm-blooded animal that feeds its young with milk
entries.definitionCN: 哺乳动物。只是拼写开头相近，词源不同

entries.definition: extremely large
very much larger than usual
of very great size; also a huge person or thing
large, heavy and solid

normalIntro.en: Mammoth is a beast so big that the creature itself became the word for size.
normalIntro.cn: mammoth 是那种大到「以兽代尺」的巨兽，它的名字后来直接变成了表示「巨大」的词。

normal.en: The woolly mammoth is the classic Ice Age image: heavy hair and curling tusks.
normal.cn: woolly mammoth 是最经典的冰期形象：厚毛和卷曲的长牙。

normal.en: In English, mammoth first meant the animal, then grew into an adjective for size.
normal.cn: 在英语里，mammoth 先指动物，后来长成一个表示尺度的形容词。

normal.en: A mammoth task is not an elephant job but a job that feels elephant-sized.
normal.cn: a mammoth task 不是给大象的活，而是大得像大象的活。

normal.en: The Russian word mammot is the link that carried the word from Siberia into English.
normal.cn: 俄语词 mammot 是西伯利亚语言与英语之间的桥梁。

normal.en: Unlike mammalian, mammoth has no link to mamma, the Latin word for breast.
normal.cn: 与 mammalian 不同，mammoth 和拉丁语 mamma（乳房）没有关系。

abstract.en: See a wall of shaggy brown hair and two white tusks in the snow.
abstract.cn: 想象雪里出现一堵蓬松的褐色毛墙和两根白长牙。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger the size of a bus, all columns and zeroes.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账单大得像公交车，满是栏格和零。

abstract.en: Imagine a mountain of boxes on a desk marked for one person.
abstract.cn: 想象办公桌上堆着一座箱子山，只为一个人的活计。

examples.en: Researchers found mammoth bones under the melting permafrost.
examples.cn: 研究人员在融化的永久冻土下发现了猛犸象的骨骼。

examples.en: Translating the entire archive is a mammoth job.
examples.cn: 翻译整批档案是一项浩大的工程。

examples.en: The stadium was a mammoth structure of concrete and glass.
examples.cn: 这座体育场是一座混凝土与玻璃筑成的庞然大物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈冒死」——妈妈冒着大雪也要护住小猛犸象，可见它有多大。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自西伯利亚某语言，经俄语 mammot（西伯利亚巨兽）→ 英语 mammoth；西伯利亚语的原始形式来源不确定，与拉丁语 mamma（乳房）及 mammalian 无词源关系。核心义「冰原巨象」→「巨大」。

sensesIntro.en: Mammoth begins as the name of an Ice Age giant, then becomes an adjective for sheer size, for huge tasks, for oversized things and for an old intensifier.
sensesIntro.cn: mammoth 起于冰期巨兽的名字，再变成表达尺度的形容词，用于巨大事物、浩大任务，以及一个旧式的程度加强词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shaggy Ice Age elephant with curling tusks, dwarfing everything in the snow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头披厚毛、长螺旋长牙的冰期巨象，把雪原上其他一切都衬得渺小。

branches.en: The extinct elephant is the literal, original sense.
branches.cn: 已灭绝的巨象是最早的字面义项。

branches.en: Extreme size in amounts and bills comes from the animal scale.
branches.cn: 数量与账单上的极端巨大源自巨象的尺度。

branches.en: Huge difficulty is size turned into effort.
branches.cn: 艰巨浩大是把尺度转成投入。

branches.en: An enormous building is the noun kept as a shape word.
branches.cn: 庞然大物是名词保留形状含义的用法。

branches.en: The old intensifier is the adjective pushed further into degree.
branches.cn: 旧式加强词是把形容词进一步推向程度。

intro.en: Mammoth is a borrowed word rather than a Latin construction; its English growth happens by compounding with woolly and by the suffix -like.
intro.cn: mammoth 是借词，不是拉丁语构词；它在英语中的生长靠与 woolly 的复合，以及后缀 -like。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestry; appearances such as mammoth and mammalian are unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语渊源；mammoth 与 mammalian 只是外形相像，并不相关。

items.example: A mammoth once roamed these plains.
items.exampleCN: 猛犸象曾在这片平原上漫游。

items.example: They staged a mammoth show.
items.exampleCN: 他们办了一场规模巨大的演出。

items.example: Many mammoths crossed this valley.
items.exampleCN: 许多猛犸象曾穿过这道山谷。

items.example: The woolly mammoth lived in cold steppe.
items.exampleCN: 披毛猛犸象生活在寒冷的草原上。

items.meaning: the hairy mammoth of the Ice Age
items.example: Woolly mammoth remains are found in Siberia.
items.exampleCN: 西伯利亚出土过披毛猛犸象的遗骸。

items.example: The suffix -like forms mammoth-like.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -like 构成 mammoth-like。

items.example: A mammoth-like crane lifted the beam.
items.exampleCN: 一台巨象般大小的吊车吊起了钢梁。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms enormous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 enormous。

items.example: The enormous hall held the skeleton.
items.exampleCN: 巨大的展厅里放着那副骨架。

definition_zh: 普通话；柑橘（柑橘类小果）；官员；高级官员
definition_en: the standard form of Chinese spoken in the north and used officially, a small sweet citrus fruit, or a high government official
core_image: 一个矮胖的橙色柑橘，皮薄易剥，果肉分瓣
scene: 老师要求学生用普通话朗读课文。The teacher asked the students to read the text aloud in mandarin.
sceneCN: 这里 mandarin 是「普通话」（第 1 个义项：中国通行的标准口语）；句意：老师要求学生用普通话朗读课文。

derivatives.zh: 由 mandarin（官员）加后缀 -ate（集合名词）构成，义为「官僚集团；官场」。
由 mandarin（官员）加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「官僚作风；官腔」。
由 mandarin（官员）加后缀 -al（形容词后缀）构成，义为「官僚的；官场的」。

senses.title: The standard spoken Chinese
senses.definition: the standard form of Chinese, based on northern speech and used in schools and official life
senses.definitionCN: 以北方话为基础、用于教学与公务的标准汉语口语
senses.example: Most people in the city speak mandarin at work.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市里大多数人工作时说普通话。
senses.why: The word first named the speech of the Ming and Qing officials, and the official language later became the national standard.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指明清官员所用的官话，官场语言后来成为全国通行的标准语，于是由「官话」长成「普通话」。

senses.title: A small sweet citrus fruit
senses.definition: a small citrus fruit with a loose orange skin and sweet segments
senses.definitionCN: 一种小型的柑橘类水果，果皮橙色、易剥，果肉分瓣而甜
senses.example: She peeled a mandarin and shared the segments.
senses.exampleCN: 她剥了一个柑橘，把果瓣分给大家。
senses.why: The fruit was named after the bright orange coat of Chinese officials, which the peel resembles.
senses.whyCN: 这种橙色小果的颜色接近中国官员的橙色袍服，人们便用它来命名水果，于是在核心意象上从「柑橘」直接长出这一义。

senses.title: A senior official
senses.definition: a high-ranking official in an imperial Chinese government, or a powerful civil servant elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 中国古代的高级官员，或泛指权力很大的文职官僚
senses.example: A mandarin in the capital drafted the new decree.
senses.exampleCN: 京城里一位高级官员起草了新的法令。
senses.why: The word goes back to Portuguese mandarim, which described the officials of imperial China, so the official is the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自葡萄牙语对明清中国官员的称呼，官员是最初的义项，也是后面普通话与柑橘两个义项的起点。

senses.title: An obscure or pedantic language
senses.definition: the specialised and hard-to-understand language used by officials or powerful experts
senses.definitionCN: 官员或权势群体使用的、外人难以听懂的专门话术
senses.example: The report was full of mandarin and almost impossible to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告满是官腔，几乎无法看懂。
senses.why: Because only officials once spoke the official register, its difficult style became a byword for power hidden in words.
senses.whyCN: 旧时只有官员掌握官场语体，这种晦涩作风于是被借来比喻任何「用话术维持权力」的语言，从官员义引申出贬义。

intro.en: Mandarin came into English through Portuguese mandarim, which named the officials of imperial China.
intro.cn: mandarin 经葡萄牙语 mandarim 进入英语，原指中国帝制时代的官员。

items.en: Mantrin means a counsellor or adviser.
items.cn: 梵语 mantrin 意为谋士、顾问。

items.en: Menteri means a minister or official.
items.cn: 马来语 menteri 意为大臣、官员。

items.en: Portugal traders used mandarim for Chinese officials.
items.cn: 十六世纪葡萄牙商人用 mandarim 称呼中国官员。

items.en: English borrowed mandarin for officials and later for their language.
items.cn: 英语借入 mandarin 指官员，随后又指官员所说的话。

items.en: Modern English also uses mandarin for the standard Chinese speech and for a citrus fruit.
items.cn: 现代英语中 mandarin 还指标准汉语口语与一种柑橘。

note.en: Mandarin sits with its official-root relatives and with Chinese language terms and citrus names.
note.cn: mandarin 与同源的「官员」词族相邻，也靠近汉语称谓与柑橘类词。

entries.definition: an official order or authorisation
entries.definitionCN: 授权；命令（同源于拉丁语 mandare，只是拼写相近，词形相近而用法不同）

entries.definition: a body of senior officials
bureaucratic style in speech or writing
the official standard spoken Chinese of mainland China
entries.definitionCN: 普通话（中国大陆的官方标准口语称谓）

entries.definition: the Yue variety of Chinese spoken in the south
a small sweet orange citrus fruit

normalIntro.en: Mandarin is a word about officials that grew into a language and a fruit.
normalIntro.cn: mandarin 本是关于「官员」的词，后来长成了语言名和水果名。

normal.en: Speak mandarin in class to practise the standard speech.
normal.cn: speak mandarin 就是在课堂上练习标准口语。

normal.en: Mandarin collars rise from old official robes.
normal.cn: mandarin collar 立领源自旧时官服。

normal.en: A mandarin orange is easy to peel by hand.
normal.cn: mandarin orange 就是手剥很方便的橘子。

normal.en: Historical mandarins were the literate officials of imperial China.
normal.cn: 历史上的 mandarin 是中国帝制时代读书做官的人。

normal.en: Putonghua is the mainland name for mandarin.
normal.cn: putonghua 是大陆对普通话的正式称谓。

abstract.en: Picture a long hall where every sentence is spoken in one shared tongue.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长廊，人人用同一种通行口语交谈。

abstract.en: Imagine an orange peel curling off a small fruit in one motion.
abstract.cn: 想象一片橙色果皮从小果子上整条卷落。

abstract.en: Think of an official in an orange robe reading an order aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一位穿橙色袍服的官员大声宣读命令。

examples.en: She learned mandarin during two years in Beijing.
examples.cn: 她在北京住了两年，学会了普通话。

examples.en: The market sells mandarins, lemons and limes.
examples.cn: 市场上卖柑橘、柠檬和青柠。

examples.en: The new governor was described as a modern mandarin.
examples.cn: 新总督被形容为一位现代官僚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满的任」——官满任，说的就是官员；记住 mandarin 先指官，再指官话和柑橘，这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 梵语 mantrin（谋士）→ 马来语 menteri（官员）→ 葡萄牙语 mandarim（中国官员）→ 英语 mandarin（官员→官话→普通话；柑橘）。

sensesIntro.en: Mandarin starts from the imperial official, passes through the official speech that became standard Chinese, and branches out to the language of power and a citrus fruit.
sensesIntro.cn: mandarin 从帝制时代的官员出发，经「官话」过渡到标准汉语，又分出「官僚话术」与一种柑橘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bright orange citrus fruit that peels easily.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个橙色、皮薄易剥的小柑橘。

branches.en: The official speech turned into the standard spoken Chinese.
branches.cn: 官话演变为普通话。

branches.en: The bright citrus fruit carries the colour image.
branches.cn: 明亮的柑橘承载颜色意象。

branches.en: The original sense is the imperial official.
branches.cn: 最初的义项就是帝制官员。

branches.en: Both the standard language and bureaucratic jargon are forms of official speech.
branches.cn: 标准汉语与官腔都是「官话」的变体。

branches.en: The orange of the fruit echoes the orange robe of the official.
branches.cn: 果实的橙色呼应官员的橙色袍服。

intro.en: Mandarin is a borrowed noun, and English builds mandarinate and mandarinism on it with the suffixes -ate and -ism.
intro.cn: mandarin 是外来借词，英语用后缀 -ate 和 -ism 在它基础上构成 mandarinate 与 mandarinism。

latinIntro.en: The word reached English through Portuguese and Malay rather than Latin, though Rome is where the fruit name first appears.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经葡萄牙语和马来语进入英语，并非直接来自拉丁语；但水果义最早出自罗马的柑橘园。

items.example: Mandarin arrived through the Portuguese form.
items.exampleCN: mandarin 经葡萄牙语形式传入。

items.example: Early English used it for officials.
items.exampleCN: 早期英语用它指官员。

items.example: The official speech became the standard language.
items.exampleCN: 官话变成了标准语言。

items.example: The orange fruit takes the same name.
items.exampleCN: 这种橙色水果用了同一个名字。

items.meaning: an office or body of people
items.meaningCN: 表示职位或群体的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ate forms mandarinate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成 mandarinate。

items.example: Mandarinate means the ruling bureaucrats.
items.exampleCN: mandarinate 指掌权的官僚群体。

items.meaningCN: 表示作风或做法的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms mandarinism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 mandarinism。

items.example: Mandarinism describes stiff official language.
items.exampleCN: mandarinism 描述生硬的官方语言。

items.example: The mandarin collar rises around the neck.
items.exampleCN: mandarin collar 是绕颈竖起的领子。

definition_zh: 授权；委任；命令；强制要求；授权令
definition_en: the authority given to a government or group by voters, a formal order, or to give someone the power or duty to do something
core_image: 一只只手把印章交到某人掌心，权柄由此交付
scene: 选民投票后，新政府获得了改革的授权。After the election, the new government received a mandate to reform the tax system.
sceneCN: 这里 mandate 是「授权；委任」（第 1 个义项：选民赋予政府行动的正当权力）；句意：选民投票后，新政府获得了改革的授权。

derivatives.zh: 由 mandate 过去分词转化为形容词，义为「受委任的；强制规定的」。
由词根 mand-（命令）加后缀 -atory（具有……性质的）构成，义为「强制的；义务的」。
由 mandate 加后缀 -or（施动者）构成，义为「委托人；下达指令者」。

senses.title: Authority given by voters
senses.definition: the right to act, given to a government or group by the people who elected it
senses.definitionCN: 选民或成员赋予政府或团体的行动权力
senses.example: The party claimed a clear mandate after the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票之后，该党声称获得了明确授权。
senses.why: Latin mandare means to hand over, so a mandate is power handed from the people into the hands of those who govern.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mandare 意为「交到手上」，所以授权就是把权力从选民手中交到执政者手里。

senses.title: A formal order
senses.definition: an official instruction that must be obeyed, often issued by a court or a superior body
senses.definitionCN: 必须服从的正式指示，常由法院或上级机构发出
senses.example: The court issued a mandate ordering the company to pay.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下达命令，要求该公司付款。
senses.why: Once power is handed over, the order that arrives in the holder hand is itself called a mandate, a written command.
senses.whyCN: 权力被交付之后，送到对方手上的书面命令本身就叫 mandate，于是从「授权」自然长出具身化的「命令」。

senses.title: To require officially
senses.definition: to make something a legal or official requirement, or to be made such a requirement
senses.definitionCN: 使某事成为法律或官方的硬性要求
senses.example: New rules mandate that every ship carry enough lifeboats.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定强制要求每艘船都配备足够的救生艇。
senses.why: The verb turns the written command into an action: an authority mandates what others must do.
senses.whyCN: 动词义把书面命令变成动作：有权者发出强制要求，他人必须执行，这正是授权者的权力在动用。

senses.title: A territory entrusted to another state
senses.definition: a former colony placed under the administration of another country by an international body
senses.definitionCN: 由国际机构交给另一国管理的原殖民地
senses.example: After the war, the region became a mandate of the winning power.
senses.exampleCN: 战后，该地区成了战胜国的托管地。
senses.why: In the early twentieth century, the League of Nations handed whole territories to member states, the most literal handing over of all.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪初国际联盟把整片领土交托给成员国管理，这是「把东西交到手上」最字面的一次延伸，于是衍生出托管地义。

intro.en: Mandate comes from Latin mandare, meaning to put into someone hand, and so to order or commission.
intro.cn: mandate 来自拉丁语 mandare，本义是「交到某人手上」，进而引申为命令、委托。

items.en: Manus means hand, and mandare means to give into the hand.
items.cn: manus 意为手，mandare 意为交到手上。

items.en: Mandatum means a command or commission, an entrusted thing.
items.cn: mandatum 意为命令、委托，即被交托之事。

items.en: Mandat carries the sense of command and authority.
items.cn: 古法语 mandat 带出命令与权威之义。

items.en: English mandate names a command or a commission.
items.cn: 英语 mandate 指命令或委任。

items.en: Political mandate names the authority won at an election.
items.cn: 政治用语中 mandate 指选举赢得的授权。

items.en: The League of Nations used mandate for entrusted territories, and the verb now means to require officially.
items.cn: 国际联盟用 mandate 指托管领土，动词义也演变为「强制规定」。

note.en: Mandate shares the Latin mandare root with mandatory and mandator, and stands close to other words for orders and authority.
note.cn: mandate 与 mandatory、mandator 共享拉丁词根 mandare，也靠近一批表示命令与权威的词。

entries.definition: required by law or rule
a person who gives a commission
officially required or entrusted
official permission to do something
an official instruction to carry out a task
an official instruction about what to do

normalIntro.en: Mandate is a handover: power, orders and duties are put into someone hand.
normalIntro.cn: mandate 是一个交接：权力、命令与义务被交到某人手里。

normal.en: Election results give a government its mandate.
normal.cn: 选举结果赋予一个政府授权。

normal.en: The verb mandate often appears in passive form with by: mandated by law.
normal.cn: 动词 mandate 常用于被动形式 with by：mandated by law。

normal.en: Mandatory is the adjective built on the same root as mandate.
normal.cn: mandatory 是与 mandate 同根的形容词。

normal.en: A mandate and a commission both mean a task entrusted to someone.
normal.cn: mandate 与 commission 都表示交托给某人的任务。

normal.en: The Latin root mand- also appears in command and demand.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 mand- 也出现在 command 与 demand 中。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd pressing an official seal into a leader open hand.
abstract.cn: 想象人群把一枚官印按进领导人摊开的手掌。

abstract.en: Visualise a sealed letter carried down a long corridor and delivered.
abstract.cn: 设想一封印好的信沿长廊送到收信人手中。

abstract.en: Think of a rulebook so heavy that nobody can lift it, only obey.
abstract.cn: 想象一本沉重得没人能举起、只能服从的规则手册。

examples.en: The minister said the vote gave her a mandate for reform.
examples.cn: 部长说这次投票赋予她改革授权。

examples.en: Local law mandates that all new buildings have fire exits.
examples.cn: 当地法律强制要求所有新建筑都设消防出口。

examples.en: The court mandate reached the company on Friday.
examples.cn: 法院的命令在周五送达了该公司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满的」——被「授权」之后，手上就多了一项满当的职责；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 manus（手）+ dare（给）→ mandare（交到手上；命令、委托）→ mandatum → 法语 mandat → 英语 mandate，核心义「把权力或任务交到你手上」。

sensesIntro.en: Mandate moves from the power handed to a government by voters, to the written orders and required duties that follow, and finally to whole territories entrusted to another state.
sensesIntro.cn: mandate 从「选民交给政府的权力」出发，延伸为随之而来的书面命令与强制义务，最后指整片交给别国管理的托管地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal pressed into an open hand, power changing hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章按进摊开的手掌，权力易手。

branches.en: Voters hand authority to a government.
branches.cn: 选民把权力交给政府。

branches.en: The order that arrives in the hand is the command.
branches.cn: 送到手上的书面命令。

branches.en: The verb turns the command into a binding requirement.
branches.cn: 动词义把命令变成强制要求。

branches.en: An international mandate entrusts a whole territory.
branches.cn: 国际托管把整片领土交托出去。

branches.en: Both a court order and a legal requirement press duty on someone.
branches.cn: 法院命令与法定要求都把义务压到某人身上。

intro.en: Mandate is built from the Latin root mand- meaning to hand over and to order, and English shapes mandated, mandatory and mandator around it.
intro.cn: mandate 由拉丁词根 mand-（交付、命令）构成，英语围绕它构成 mandated、mandatory 与 mandator。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus means hand and dare means to give, so mandare means to give into the hand, and mandatum is the thing entrusted.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为手，dare 意为给，所以 mandare 意为交到手上，mandatum 则是被交托之物。

items.example: Manus gives the hand in the core image.
items.exampleCN: manus 提供核心意象中的「手」。

items.example: Dare adds the giving to the hand.
items.exampleCN: dare 为「手」加上「给」的动作。

items.example: Mandare means to put into the hand.
items.exampleCN: mandare 意为交到手上。

items.example: Mandatum is the entrusted task.
items.exampleCN: mandatum 是受托的任务。

items.meaning: a thing given or an act
items.meaningCN: 表示事物或动作的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ate forms the Latin past participle.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成拉丁语过去分词。

items.example: Mandated describes a required duty.
items.exampleCN: mandated 描述被强制规定的义务。

items.example: The suffix -ory helps form mandatory.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ory 帮助构成 mandatory。

items.example: Mandatory means you must do it.
items.exampleCN: mandatory 表示必须去做。

items.example: The suffix -or forms mandator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 mandator。

items.example: The mandator sets the task.
items.exampleCN: 委托人下达任务。

definition_zh: 强制的；义务的；必须的；受委任的
definition_en: required by law or by an official rule, so that it must be done
core_image: 一条横在路口的红绳，谁都必须停下、出示通行证
scene: 出发前，学校请家长填写完整的疫苗接种记录。Before the school trip, every parent had to show a mandatory vaccination record.
sceneCN: 这里 mandatory 是「强制的；必须的」（第 1 个义项：由规定要求、不得不做）；句意：出发前，每位家长都必须出示强制要求的疫苗接种记录。

pos.zh: （国际联盟）受委任的人；强制条款

derivatives.zh: 由 mandatory 加后缀 -ly（副词后缀）构成，义为「强制地；必须地」。
与 mandatory 同源的动词与名词，义为「授权；命令」。
由 mandate 过去分词转化而来，义为「受委任的；强制规定的」。

senses.title: Required by law or rule
senses.definition: ordered by a law or official rule, so that doing it is not a choice
senses.definitionCN: 由法律或官方规则规定，做与不做没有选择余地
senses.example: Wearing a helmet is mandatory on the site.
senses.exampleCN: 在工地上戴头盔是强制性的。
senses.why: The Latin root mandare means to command, so mandatory marks whatever has been commanded by those in power.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 mandare 意为命令，mandatory 标记的就是权势者已下令必须做的事。

senses.title: Fixed by a legal penalty
senses.titleCN: 法定必需的；法定最低的
senses.definition: fixed by law and not left to a judge or an individual to decide
senses.definitionCN: 由法律固定规定，不由法官或个人酌情决定
senses.example: The judge had to impose the mandatory minimum sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官不得不判处法定最低刑期。
senses.why: When the command is written into law in exact terms, the adjective describes rules that leave no room for discretion.
senses.whyCN: 当命令被写进法律条文并明确量化时，这个形容词就描述没有裁量空间的规则，所以长出了「法定固定」义。

senses.title: Entrusted with an office
senses.definition: holding a position or power assigned by a higher authority, especially in international law
senses.definitionCN: 担任上级机构交托的职位或权力，尤用于国际法语境
senses.example: The mandated power reported on the territory each year.
senses.exampleCN: 受委任统治国每年就该领地提交报告。
senses.why: The older legal sense keeps the literal image, an agent holding a task that someone else has placed in his hands.
senses.whyCN: 较早的法律义保留字面画面：受托者手里拿着别人交给他的任务，于是从「强制」回到「受托」的源头。

intro.en: Mandatory comes from Latin mandatorius, from mandatum, a command, which English also took as mandate.
intro.cn: mandatory 来自拉丁语 mandatorius，源于 mandatum（命令），英语也把 mandatum 借为 mandate。

items.en: Mandare means to hand over and to command.
items.cn: mandare 意为交付与命令。

items.en: Mandatorius describes what belongs to a command or a commissioner.
items.cn: mandatorius 描述与命令或委托人相关之事。

items.en: Legal Latin uses mandatorius for binding instructions.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语法律文本用 mandatorius 指有约束力的指令。

items.en: Mandatory enters English with the sense of commanded.
items.cn: mandatory 以「受命」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word spreads as a label for legally required actions.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐用来标注法律要求的行动。

items.en: Modern use adds mandatory sentences and mandatory training.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了法定刑期与强制培训等表达。

note.en: Mandatory shares the mand- root with mandate and mandator and sits among words for rules and duties.
note.cn: mandatory 与 mandate、mandator 共享 mand- 词根，并处在表示规则与义务的词里。

entries.definition: an official order or authority
a person who gives a commission
in a required way
required by law or a rule
necessary because a rule or moral duty says so
that must be obeyed
entries.definitionCN: 有约束力的；必须遵守的

normalIntro.en: Mandatory is the adjective of command: it labels what has been ordered and cannot be skipped.
normalIntro.cn: mandatory 是「命令」的形容词：它标记已被下令、不能跳过的事。

normal.en: Mandatory and mandatory sentences both come from mandate.
normal.cn: mandatory 与法定刑期表达都源于 mandate。

normal.en: Compare optional: optional means you may choose, mandatory means you must.
normal.cn: 对比 optional：optional 表示可以选，mandatory 表示必须做。

normal.en: We say mandatory for all, not mandatory to all.
normal.cn: 习惯说 mandatory for all，而不是 mandatory to all。

normal.en: Compulsory and obligatory are near synonyms in IELTS writing.
normal.cn: 在雅思写作中，compulsory 与 obligatory 是近义替换。

normal.en: The root mand- also shows in command and demand.
normal.cn: 词根 mand- 也出现在 command 与 demand 里。

abstract.en: Picture a red rope across a road that everyone must stop at.
abstract.cn: 想象路口横着一条红绳，人人都必须停下。

abstract.en: Think of a giant stamp that marks every document as required.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚巨大的印章，把每份文件都盖成「必需」。

abstract.en: Visualise a gate that opens only when the rule is obeyed.
abstract.cn: 设想一扇只有在遵守规则时才打开的门。

examples.en: Attendance at the safety briefing is mandatory for all staff.
examples.cn: 全体员工都必须参加安全简报。

examples.en: Many schools have made uniforms mandatory.
examples.cn: 许多学校已经强制要求穿校服。

examples.en: The law sets a mandatory minimum of two years.
examples.cn: 法律规定的最低刑期为两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满的」——规矩「满」得没得挑，只能照做，就是「强制的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mandare（交到手上；命令）→ mandatorius（与命令相关的）→ 英语 mandatory，核心义「已被下令、没有商量余地」。

sensesIntro.en: Mandatory begins with anything required by law, extends to rules fixed in exact legal terms, and keeps an older sense of holding an entrusted office.
sensesIntro.cn: mandatory 从「法律要求的必须之事」出发，延伸到「法律明文固定的规则」，并保留「担任受托职位」的较早义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red rope across a road that nobody is allowed to step over.
core.cn: 核心意象：路口横着一条没人能跨过的红绳。

branches.en: Whatever has been commanded becomes a required action.
branches.cn: 凡被下令之事都成为必须完成的动作。

branches.en: A command written into law leaves no room for discretion.
branches.cn: 写进法律的命令不再有裁量空间。

branches.en: The earliest sense is holding an entrusted office.
branches.cn: 最早的义项是担任受托职位。

branches.en: Both daily requirements and fixed penalties forbid free choice.
branches.cn: 日常要求与固定刑罚都取消了自由选择。

branches.en: A mandated role is a task handed over in the same way a legal rule is.
branches.cn: 受委任的职位与法定规则一样，都是被交到手上的任务。

intro.en: Mandatory is built on the Latin root mand- meaning to command or entrust, with the adjective suffix -ory added to the stem.
intro.cn: mandatory 建在拉丁词根 mand-（命令、委托）之上，词干后接形容词后缀 -ory。

latinIntro.en: Latin mandare means to hand over and to order, and mandatorius describes what belongs to a command or a commissioner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mandare 意为交付与命令，mandatorius 描述与命令或委托人相关之物。

items.example: The root mand- links mandate and mandatory.
items.exampleCN: 词根 mand- 连接 mandate 与 mandatory。

items.example: Mandare carries the idea of ordering.
items.exampleCN: mandare 带有「下令」之意。

items.meaningCN: 表示功能或性质的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ory forms a describing adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ory 构成描述性形容词。

items.example: Mandatory means it must be done.
items.exampleCN: mandatory 表示必须做到。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mandatorily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 mandatorily。

items.example: Mandatorily describes how a rule applies.
items.exampleCN: mandatorily 描述规则的适用方式。

items.example: A mandate is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: mandate 是其背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms mandated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 mandated。

items.example: Mandated duties are set by an authority.
items.exampleCN: 受命义务由权威机构设定。
